### R-USSHORT-CUT5-OFFLINE-SOURCES-PIT-DUPLICATE-COVERAGE-AND-AUTH-GAP - four source producers admit post-open/duplicated facts and their schemas do not freeze PIT or authorization semantics

- **Status**: **resolved** (Codex independent full re-review PASS 2026-07-01; OFFLINE). The four producer contracts close the registered PIT/chronology, duplicate identity, checked-empty provenance, schema-policy, authorization, and hostile-value classes; live fetch/Pass2/DataHub/production remain gated and were not exercised.
- **Severity**: **P1** before any producer is wired into Pass2, hard-veto, catalyst/risk downgrade, data-context, or official output.
- **Scope / PIT label**: US-short Cut 5-a/5-b/5-c/5-d offline producers only: `engine/us_short_sec_offering_audit.py`, `engine/us_short_massive_financials.py`, `engine/us_short_fmp_analyst_grades.py`, `engine/us_short_massive_news.py`; their four dated binding JSON files, four binding schemas, and four direct test files. Read-only adjacency covered `engine/us_short_hard_veto.py`, `engine/us_short_eligibility_gate.py::canonical_us_ticker`, `docs/us_short_system_design.md` §2.1/§3.1/§3.3/§3.5/§4.2/§5/§10/§18.2, the probe summary/raw-shape dependency, and route docs. Cut 4 remained excluded/open under its own ID. Live fetch/runners, provider calls, Pass2/data-context wiring, DataHub, production/ship-gate, broker/order, A-share, A-long, and US-long were not run or authorized.
- **Finding A - all four producers use an ET-date gate instead of the reviewed pre-open instant, and event chronology is incomplete**: each producer validates `observed_at` only by `ET date <= as_of`; the happy fixtures themselves use `12:00 ET` on the decision date. Direct probes showed a post-open provenance observation still emits an active offering, a financial record, an analyst action summary, and a news summary. Cut 5-b and 5-d additionally carry event instants (`acceptance_datetime` / `published_utc`) but compare only their ET date, so an event at `20:00Z` (16:00 ET) is emitted even when provenance claims it was observed at `08:00 ET`, an impossible event-after-observation chronology. Cut 5-a discards SEC `acceptanceDateTime` entirely even though the probe established it is available, retaining only `filing_date`; a same-day filing accepted after the 09:30 decision open is therefore indistinguishable from premarket evidence. This conflicts with the owner half-open window `[prior close, decision open)` and can inject same-session look-ahead facts into audit/catalyst output.
- **Finding B - repeated provider rows and weak identifiers can fabricate counts / evidence**: no producer enforces a source-row identity or duplicate policy. Exact duplicate FMP grade rows produce two upgrades and `net=2`; exact duplicate Massive news IDs produce `news_count=2`, `positive=2`, and `net_sentiment=2`; duplicate financial periods are emitted twice; duplicate SEC accessions are repeated in contributing provenance. Firm/publisher variants such as `BankX` vs ` bankx ` and `Pub` vs ` pub ` count as distinct, while whitespace-only offering accession is accepted as traceable. Massive news requires `id` on input but drops it from output records, preventing reverse lookup/dedup at the consumer. This directly affects the §5.2 collective-downgrade basis and future catalyst/advisory counts.
- **Finding C - checked-empty coverage collapses to the same output as unknown/unprovided**: after validating full/ok provenance, every producer `continue`s when it has zero relevant/PIT-fit rows. The result is empty `signals/records`, empty `provenance`, and empty `excluded`—identical to no ticker input at all. For 5-a this is safety-critical: a fully audited "no offering" result loses the coverage proof that distinguishes clean from an unqueried/unknown candidate, contrary to §3.3. The same collapse prevents catalyst/financial consumers from applying the documented data-quality distinction between checked-neutral and missing coverage.
- **Finding D - the claimed frozen bindings do not freeze PIT or authorization, and are unrouted**: all four schemas describe themselves as const-pinning load-bearing PIT/offline semantics, but `pit_rule` and key derivation/value-contract prose are merely arbitrary strings. Replacing every `pit_rule` with text allowing post-open/duplicate evidence yields zero schema errors. `authorization_note` is optional, non-const, and can be removed or changed to "live fetch, DataHub and production are authorized" with zero errors; there is no machine authorization-boundary object. Tests validate only the genuine artifact and selected engine constants, with no hostile schema mutations. None of the four binding/engine/test groups has a `docs/README.md` route row. Cut 5-b also depends on the quarterly/annual raw re-probe omitted from the tracked probe summary under `R-USSHORT-CUT5-PASS2-PROBE-TRACEABILITY-AND-ARTIFACT-BINDING-GAP`; its source-shape basis is therefore not durable yet.
- **Why material**: these modules are the future boundary between provider evidence and a hard-veto/catalyst/risk layer. Post-open or event-after-observation facts are PIT contamination; duplicate rows can manufacture collective signal strength; checked-empty collapse can silently turn an unaudited safety field into apparent clean absence; and optional prose cannot enforce the no-live/no-DataHub/no-production boundary required before cross-module consumption.
- **Required repair**: repair the four producers as one defect class but keep their file/commit boundaries reviewable and offline. (1) Use the canonical decision-open instant and enforce `observed_at < decision_open` for every source; require complete event chronology. For financials/news, enforce event instant `<= observed_at < decision_open`; for SEC offerings, carry and validate `acceptanceDateTime` (or conservatively exclude same-day filings without a pre-open instant); for date-only grades, bind the record date to the observed instant and exclude any same-day record not provably observed pre-open. Add exact-open, one-before/after, UTC-Z/offset/DST, event-after-observation, future, stale, and positive controls for every family. (2) Freeze source-row identities and reject or deterministically deduplicate exact/canonical duplicates before any count/status/output: accession for SEC, a documented fiscal-period/filing identity for financials, a stable composite/event identity for grades, and Massive `id` for news. Carry those identities into output provenance/records; normalize or reject whitespace/case-only firm/publisher variants according to a frozen policy; reject blank trace IDs. (3) Emit an explicit per-ticker checked status/coverage record for full+ok zero-event/zero-fit results so consumers can distinguish checked-neutral/clean from unknown/unprovided; retain safety-audit provenance for 5-a even when no offering exists. (4) Replace free prose gates with const-pinned machine contracts for PIT operator/exclusivity/chronology, identity/duplicate policy, checked-empty disposition, structured lineage, and an explicit all-false live/network/raw/runner/DataHub/production/ship-gate authorization boundary. Add adversarial schema tests for each mutation and triangulate every load-bearing field to behavior. (5) Close or explicitly depend on the repaired probe evidence for 5-b, and add four thin route rows (or one concise grouped owner row if within route-row cap) to `docs/README.md`. Do not fetch data, wire Pass2/data-context, change hard-veto scoring, build DataHub/production, claim ship-gate evidence, or cross market lanes.

- **Status**: **resolved** (Codex re-review PASS 2026-07-01; committed `55b21c4`; OFFLINE). Cut 3b-local identity/clock legs and the account-converter mirror are closed under one delegated `canonical_us_ticker` policy.

Dirty Cut 2 momentum files were excluded. Provider/live discovery, member-list assembly, exact member-to-benchmark daily-date alignment, R3/Pass2, DataHub, production/ship-gate, broker/order paths, A-share, A-long, and US-long were not reviewed or authorized.
- **Technical finding A - member identity is not validated or made unique**: `provisional_theme_heat_block` iterates raw `members` keys and appends every valid series without applying the repo's `canonical_us_ticker` policy or detecting post-canonical collisions. A direct probe supplied the same security as `AAPL`, `aapl`, ` AAPL `, `AaPl`, and `AAPL `. The producer reported `member_count=5`, all four price/count flags `True`, and the adjacent `market_confirmation_passed(..., stock_is_strong=True)` returned `True`; one security therefore satisfied the design's minimum-member/self-confirmation guard and at least three-of-seven market-confirmation gate. A second probe used five identities that the shared US ticker policy rejects (`000001.SZ`, `600000.SH`, `430047.BJ`, integer `123`, and `None`); Cut 3b still counted all five and emitted the same four `True` flags. Thus malformed or cross-market identities can manufacture breadth, volume, leader-RS, and member-count evidence.
- **Technical finding B - the remaining public identity/clock shape is not fail-closed**: `theme_id` is accepted as any dict key even though the output contract says string IDs. Two insufficient themes keyed by integer `1` and string `"x"` reach `sorted(insufficient_themes)` and raise a raw `TypeError`, while JSON-like numeric/string key combinations can also produce an ambiguous output identity space. `_parse_dated_series` checks only truthiness for `session` and `adjustment_mode`; all series carrying whitespace-only values (`"   "`) are treated as one valid decision clock and produce full metrics/flags. The strict date parser, PIT future cut, ascending unique axis, positive-close boundary, tail-only volume window, and non-uniform nonblank clock rejection did hold under direct probes; exact daily-date alignment remains explicitly gated to the future assembly layer and is not part of this finding.
- **Why material**: §4.3 requires a frozen member list, independent market confirmation, at least three of seven confirmation items, and a strong stock before a provisional theme can compete for the US-short theme lane. The current pure producer can turn one aliased ticker, A-share codes, or non-ticker keys into five independent members and directly satisfy four confirmation items. That is evidence contamination rather than a cosmetic validation issue. The malformed theme-ID crash is an availability failure at the same public boundary, and whitespace-only clock fields undermine the Cut 3b claim that scored evidence has a meaningful uniform decision clock. Existing 28 focused tests use distinct ticker-shaped member keys and nonblank metadata, so all focused/adjacent/full suites remain green while these probes reproduce.
- **Required repair**: close the entire public identity/clock class in this Cut 3b slice. (1) Apply the repo's single US ticker canonicalization policy before any member is counted; reject invalid/non-string/A-share identities, and fail closed on post-canonical collisions instead of silently deduplicating or counting aliases. Only canonical unique US identities may contribute to `member_count`, breadth, volume, leader RS, heat, or flags. (2) Require `theme_id` to be a nonblank string under one documented normalization policy and detect normalization collisions; malformed IDs must produce the module's deliberate fail-closed behavior, never a raw mixed-type sort crash or ambiguous serialized key. (3) Require `session` and `adjustment_mode` to be meaningful nonblank canonical metadata (at minimum reject whitespace-only and leading/trailing-whitespace drift) before adding a series to the uniform clock. (4) Add adversarial tests for case/whitespace ticker aliases, canonical collisions, A-share codes, integer/`None`/blank member keys, valid class-share symbols, mixed/non-string/blank theme IDs, whitespace-only clock metadata, and valid uniform-clock controls; include an adjacent gate assertion proving aliases cannot supply three confirmation items. Keep the repair offline and narrow: no provider/live discovery, no member-list fetch, no exact daily-date assembly work, no Cut 2 edits, no R3/Pass2/DataHub/production/ship-gate, no broker/order path, and no A-share implementation.

No provider/live/network/DataHub/production execution was run.
- **Repair (Claude 2026-07-01; OFFLINE; fixed pending Codex; +1 independent adversarial pass)** — closes the whole identity/clock class. **A (member identity)**: `provisional_theme_heat_block` now canonicalizes every member key via the repo's single `canonical_us_ticker` in new `_canonical_members` BEFORE counting — invalid / non-string / cross-market (A-share) keys are EXCLUDED (not counted; a shrunk list is fail-closed), and two keys aliasing to the same US ticker RAISE `ProvisionalThemeHeatError` (fail-closed, never silent dedup / count-both). Only canonical UNIQUE US ids feed member_count/breadth/volume/leader_rs/heat/flags. **B (theme_id)**: new `_canonical_theme_ids` requires each `theme_id` to be a nonblank string, strip-normalizes it, and raises on a non-string/blank ID or a normalization collision — killing the mixed-type `sorted()` `TypeError` and the ambiguous-key space. **C (clock)**: `_parse_dated_series` now requires `session`/`adjustment_mode` to be nonblank with no leading/trailing-whitespace drift (`_nonblank_no_drift`), so a `'   '` / `' RTH '` clock drops the series (excluded from scoring AND the uniform-clock set; verified it does NOT mask a real non-uniform mismatch). **A-line — class enumerated + all covered**: {member canonical-before-count, reject invalid/non-string/A-share, alias-collision raise, only-unique-contribute} ∪ {theme_id nonblank-string, strip-normalize, collision raise, no TypeError} ∪ {session+adjustment_mode nonblank-no-drift}. The already-closed sibling industry non-positive close finding was not reopened. Provider/live discovery feeds, member-list freezing data layer, R3 seam, Pass2, DataHub, production/ship-gate, broker/order paths, A-share, A-long, and US-long were excluded.
- **Technical finding**: `_theme_raw_metrics` computes `volume_confirm_frac` over only members with valid `vol_surge`: `surges = [m["vol_surge"] for m in members if m["vol_surge"] is not None]`, then `sum(s > VOL_SURGE_RATIO) / len(surges)`. Direct probe with a 5-member provisional theme where all members had valid rising closes but only one member carried volume data, and that one member had a volume surge, returned `member_count=5`, `volume_confirm_frac=1.0`, `theme_volume_confirm_frac=True`, all four price/count confirmation flags `True`, `theme_heat=100.0`, and downstream `market_confirmation_passed(..., stock_is_strong=True) == True`.
- **Why material**: §4.3 uses `theme_volume_confirm_frac` as one of seven market-confirmation items for a provisional cross-sector theme. Missing volume coverage is a data-quality gap, not evidence that the whole theme is volume-confirmed. The current denominator lets a thinly covered theme convert one covered member into 100% volume confirmation, helping satisfy the ≥3-of-7 gate and compete for theme seats. Existing focused tests cover all-volume-missing degrade and zero-volume days, but not partial coverage, so the current suites stayed green while the fail-open reproduced.
- **Required repair**: make volume confirmation coverage-aware and fail-safe. Either compute `volume_confirm_frac` over all usable price members (missing/invalid volume counts as not confirmed) or require an explicit minimum volume-coverage threshold before emitting a non-`None` volume metric/flag; in both cases partial coverage must not produce a full-confirmation flag from a one-member denominator. Add adversarial tests for 1-of-5 volume coverage with surge, below-threshold partial coverage, all-missing volume, zero-volume baseline, and the positive case where broad member volume coverage confirms. Keep the repair narrow: no discovery feed, no observed_at/member-freeze data-layer work, no provider calls, no threshold recalibration beyond the coverage semantics, no R3 seam/Pass2/DataHub/production/ship-gate, and no A-share crossing.
- **Codex verification evidence**: focused `python -m unittest tests.test_us_short_provisional_theme_heat tests.test_us_short_theme_heat tests.test_us_short_theme_block tests.test_us_short_theme_orthogonalize` ran `61 OK`; full offline `python -m unittest discover tests -p '*us_short*'` ran `2763 OK`; doc-route guards `tests.test_doc_governance_guard tests.test_readme_route_row_length tests.test_route_doc_ledger_status_consistency` ran `52 OK`; `python -m py_compile engine/us_short_provisional_theme_heat.py engine/us_short_theme_heat.py engine/us_short_theme_block.py engine/us_short_theme_orthogonalize.py` OK; `git diff --check` reported warning-only CRLF; boundary grep found no network/provider/A-share imports in the provisional producer/test. Direct thin-volume probe reproduced the failure: `volume_confirm_frac=1.0`, `theme_volume_confirm_frac=True`, all four producer flags `True`, and downstream market-confirmation gate `True`. No network/provider/live/DataHub/production execution was run.
- **Repair (Claude 2026-06-30; OFFLINE; fixed pending Codex)** — `engine/us_short_provisional_theme_heat.py::_theme_raw_metrics` now computes `volume_confirm_frac` COVERAGE-AWARE over the FULL member denominator (Required option a): `sum(1 for m in members if m["vol_surge"] is not None and m["vol_surge"] > VOL_SURGE_RATIO) / member_count` — a member with missing/invalid volume counts as NOT confirmed, so thin coverage can no longer convert one surging member into 100% confirmation. The metric is now the fraction of the THEME's members that are volume-confirmed (never a one-member denominator), so a 1-of-5 surge → 0.2 → `theme_volume_confirm_frac` flag False, removing the false contribution to the §4.3 ≥3-of-7 gate. **Whole-class enumeration (A — fixed the class, not just the probed leg)**: class = a sub-metric whose denominator is a PARTIAL member subset treated as full coverage; sole member = `volume_confirm_frac` (volume is the only optional sub-series). `breadth_up_frac` / `leader_rs` were verified FULL-coverage by construction — closes are mandatory for admission and (now strictly positive) guarantee a valid `ret_1m`/`ret_3m` for every member, so their denominators are already `member_count`; the engine has no `new_high`; the sibling industry-heat has no volume metric and the same full-coverage breadth/leader, so the class has no other member. **Tests**: 1-of-5 surge → 0.2 / flag False (exact Codex probe), 2-of-5 below-threshold → 0.4 / False, all-volume-missing → 0.0 / False, zero-volume baseline → 0.0 / False, broad 3-of-5 coverage → 0.6 / flag True (positive control). `_theme_raw_metrics` docstring updated (denominator = all members). **Verify**: focused provisional 20 OK; full offline `*us_short*` 2766 OK; doc-route guards 52 OK; py_compile OK; `git diff --check` CRLF-only; direct thin-volume probe (5 members, 1 surging) → `volume_confirm_frac=0.2`, `theme_volume_confirm_frac=False`. ### R-USSHORT-INDUSTRY-HEAT-NONPOSITIVE-CLOSE-FAILOPEN - industry heat accepts non-positive close series as heat evidence

- **Status**: resolved in reviewed working tree (Codex review PASS 2026-06-30; OFFLINE; later included in the same reviewed closeout set as the provisional-theme heat repair). Was: fixed pending Codex (Claude `修复` 2026-06-30; OFFLINE) after open (Codex review FAIL 2026-06-30; OFFLINE; US-short round-2 industry-heat producer slice only).
- **Severity**: P2 (future §4.3 / §4.2 35% theme-track block contamination before `industry_heat_score` is wired into the US-short scoring seam).
- **Scope reviewed**: `engine/us_short_industry_heat.py` and `tests/test_us_short_industry_heat.py`; read adjacent consumers `engine/us_short_theme_block.py`, `engine/us_short_theme_orthogonalize.py`, `engine/us_short_theme_heat.py`, and relevant US-short design rows to verify routing. The sibling `engine/us_short_provisional_theme_heat.py` / `tests/test_us_short_provisional_theme_heat.py` slice was explicitly not reviewed in this cycle. Provider/live extraction, FMP/Massive/SEC calls, DataHub, R3 seam, Pass2, production/ship-gate, A-share, A-long, and US-long were excluded.
- **Technical finding**: `engine/us_short_industry_heat.py::_clean_series` accepts any finite number, including `0.0` and negative closes. `_ret` later returns `None` only when a lookback base is non-positive, but the member still stays in `by_sector` and `at_new_high` is computed directly as `px[-1] >= max(px[-NEW_HIGH_WINDOW:])`. `_sector_raw_metrics` then counts that boolean into `new_high_frac`. Direct probes with three all-zero members (`[0.0] * 64`) or three negative-price members in one sector, plus a valid declining peer sector and a positive SPY benchmark, returned `sector_heat['ZERO'] == 100.0` / `sector_heat['NEG'] == 100.0` while the valid declining sector received `0.0`. The invalid members also appeared in `industry_heat_by_ticker` with `100.0`.
- **Why material**: the producer is intended to become the raw per-stock `industry_heat_score` for the 35% US-short theme-track block. A provider placeholder, parser bug, stale bad fixture, or caller-forged close series with non-positive prices can therefore create a top-ranked GICS industry heat score instead of being dropped or marked insufficient. This is not covered by the current focused tests: `_clean_series` rejects short / non-list / NaN / bool, but has no zero/negative price reverse test; the existing suites remained green while the direct probe reproduced the fail-open.
- **Required repair**: enforce a strictly positive close-series contract at the public price-series validation boundary used by `industry_heat_block` before any returns or `at_new_high` calculation. Non-positive member closes must make that member unusable; a sector made thin by dropping such members must fall to `insufficient_sectors` and emit no ticker heat, not neutral or positive heat. Add adversarial tests for all-zero and negative member series, mixed sectors that drop below `MIN_SECTOR_MEMBERS`, and retain positive controls for valid rising / declining / flat positive series plus the existing missing-benchmark degrade. If the same helper continues to clean SPY/QQQ, non-positive benchmark closes should be treated as invalid benchmark input, never as relative-strength evidence. Keep the repair narrow: no provider calls, no GICS data-layer work, no threshold recalibration, no R3 seam/Pass2/DataHub/production/ship-gate, and no A-share crossing.
- **Codex verification evidence**: focused `python -m unittest tests.test_us_short_industry_heat` ran 15 OK; `python -m py_compile engine/us_short_industry_heat.py` OK; full offline `python -m unittest discover tests -p '*us_short*'` ran 2757 OK; doc-route guards `tests.test_doc_governance_guard tests.test_readme_route_row_length tests.test_route_doc_ledger_status_consistency` ran 52 OK; `git diff --check` reported warning-only LF/CRLF. Direct non-positive-close probe reproduced the failure: `ZERO` sector heat `100.0`, `NEG` sector heat `100.0`, valid `COLD` sector heat `0.0`, with invalid tickers present in `industry_heat_by_ticker`. No network/provider/live/DataHub/production execution was run.
- **Repair (Claude 2026-06-30; OFFLINE; fixed pending Codex)** — `engine/us_short_industry_heat.py::_clean_series` now rejects any NON-POSITIVE close (`f <= 0.0`) at the price-series validation boundary, BEFORE any `_ret` / `at_new_high`, so a 0/negative-price member is unusable and cannot manufacture `new_high_frac` heat. `industry_heat_block` now tracks `seen_sectors` (every sector that appeared with a valid GICS label) and gates over it, so a sector thinned below `MIN_SECTOR_MEMBERS` by dropped members — INCLUDING one emptied entirely — falls to `insufficient_sectors` and emits no ticker heat (never neutral/positive). The same `_clean_series` cleans SPY/QQQ, so a non-positive benchmark → `None` → relative strength degrades to neutral, never used as evidence. **Whole-class enumeration (A — fixed the class, not the probed leg)**: class = non-positive close prices accepted as price evidence; (A) source-reject at `_clean_series` [probe leg: `at_new_high`], (B) member dropped, (C) thinned/emptied sector → insufficient + no heat, (D) non-positive benchmark → invalid — all four covered. **Sibling same-class fix (proactive; the unreviewed slice-4 engine, not yet a separate finding)**: `engine/us_short_provisional_theme_heat.py` shared `_clean_series` gained a `positive` flag — closes/benchmark now require `> 0` (a non-positive-close member is dropped, no longer inflating member_count/volume_confirm), volumes remain `>= 0` (a zero-volume day is valid); the identical latent leak in slice 4 is closed in the same cut. **Tests**: industry-heat all-zero + negative sectors → insufficient + no heat (exact Codex probe), sector thinned below min by non-positive, non-positive benchmark degrade, positive controls (rising/declining/flat-positive) + missing-benchmark retained; provisional non-positive-close member dropped / theme emptied → insufficient, non-positive benchmark degrade, zero-volume-valid. In-file module + `_clean_series` docstrings updated (both). **Verify**: focused industry 18 + provisional 17 = 35 OK; full offline `*us_short*` 2763 OK; doc-route guards 52 OK; py_compile (both) OK; `git diff --check` CRLF-only; direct probe (3 all-zero ZERO + 3 negative NEG + valid COLD + positive SPY) → ZERO/NEG insufficient, no ticker heat, COLD scored. No provider/live/network, GICS data-layer, threshold recalibration, R3 seam/Pass2/DataHub/production, or A-share crossing.

- **Codex closure (2026-06-30; PASS; OFFLINE)**: Re-reviewed the industry heat repair as a clean-slate current-working-tree check for the prior Required. `_clean_series` now rejects non-positive member and benchmark closes before return/new-high evidence; dropped members cannot emit ticker heat, and sectors thinned or emptied by invalid closes are listed as insufficient. Direct ZERO/NEG probes now produce no heat and no invalid ticker scores while a valid positive-price peer still scores. Same-class provisional non-positive-close boundary was checked only as a sibling boundary probe, not as full slice-4 PASS. Verification: focused industry + provisional same-class tests `35 OK`; full offline `python -m unittest discover tests -p '*us_short*'` `2763 OK`; doc-route guards `52 OK`; `py_compile` OK; `git diff --check` warning-only CRLF. ### R-USSHORT-CATALYST-ANALYST-REVISION-FRACTIONAL-COUNT-GAP - catalyst block accepts fractional analyst revision counts

- **Status**: resolved in reviewed working tree (Codex review PASS 2026-06-30; OFFLINE; auto-commit blocked by `.git/index.lock` permission denial plus environment escalation rejection). Was: fixed pending Codex (Claude `修复` 2026-06-30; OFFLINE) after open (Codex review FAIL 2026-06-30; US-short round-2 catalyst slice only).
- **Severity**: P2 (future `core_score` / Top15 contamination before the batch5->batch4 scoring seam is allowed to consume catalyst signals).
- **Scope reviewed**: `engine/us_short_catalyst.py`, `presets/us_short_catalyst_governance_20260630.json`, `schemas/us_short_catalyst_governance.schema.json`, `tests/test_us_short_catalyst.py`, and `tests/schema/test_us_short_catalyst_governance_schema.py`. Provider/live extraction, Pass2, R3 seam, DataHub, production, ship-gate, A-share, A-long, and US-long were excluded.
- **Technical finding**: `engine/us_short_catalyst.py::_revision_points` models `analyst_revision_net` as a finite number via `_finite`, even though the design/preset describe a net signed count and the governance bounds are integer thresholds. Direct probes showed fractional counts are accepted as realized catalyst evidence: `2.9 -> +8` and `3.1 -> +15`, producing catalyst scores `58.0` and `65.0`; `-1.1 -> -8` and `-3.1 -> -15`, producing `42.0` and `35.0`. `catalyst_block` records those rows as `realized=['analyst_revision_net']`, not as missing/unverified fallback.
- **Why material**: this pure engine is intended to become the 25% catalyst component of US-short `core_score`. Once the batch5->batch4 seam is wired, malformed provider/parser output or a caller bug can move rankings as if fractional analyst-revision counts were valid evidence. This is the same whole-class input-validation shape previously caught in count-like US-short fields: continuous values are valid for earnings surprise and semantic score, but analyst revision net is an event/count field and must not be parsed with the float validator.
- **Required repair**: validate `analyst_revision_net` as a strict signed integer count at the public scoring boundary. Reject bools, strings, NaN/Inf, non-integers, integer-valued floats such as `3.0` unless the contract explicitly chooses to accept them, and missing/non-dict values without scoring them. Add adversarial tests for `0.5`, `2.9`, `3.0`, `3.1`, `-1.1`, `-2.9`, `-3.0`, `-3.1`, bool, and numeric strings; retain positive controls for legal integer counts `-3`, `-1`, `0`, `1`, `3`. Keep the repair narrow: no provider calls, no FMP/SEC extraction, no Pass2/R3 seam, no DataHub, no production/ship-gate, no A-share crossing, and no threshold recalibration.
- **Codex verification evidence**: focused catalyst engine/schema tests 58 OK; full offline `*us_short*` 2723 OK; doc-route guards 52 OK; `py_compile` OK; `git diff --check` warning-only CRLF. The direct fractional-count probe above reproduced the fail-open behavior while all existing tests remained green.
- **Repair (Claude 2026-06-30; OFFLINE; fixed pending Codex)** — `engine/us_short_catalyst.py`: new `_finite_int` (strict signed int — rejects bool / str / NaN/Inf / fractional OR integer-valued float incl. `3.0`); `_revision_points` now parses `analyst_revision_net` via `_finite_int` instead of `_finite`, so a non-integer count returns `None` → `catalyst_block` records the row as EXCLUDED (not `realized`) and a row whose only signal is a bad count falls to `neutral_fallback` (the score can no longer move on a fractional count). **Whole-class enumeration (A — fixed the class, not the probed leg)**: the class = count fields validated at the scoring boundary with the float validator; in this engine the SOLE member is `analyst_revision_net`. The other numeric scoring inputs are genuinely CONTINUOUS — `earnings_surprise_pct` (%) and `semantic_advisory_score` ([-1,1]) correctly keep `_finite` (the Required confirms these are continuous; changing them would turn a positive control into a false negative) — and the governance `bucket_bounds_net` integer thresholds were already strict-int via `_check_subdict` (no bug). Module + `_revision_points` in-file docstrings updated to state the strict-int count. **Tests**: `_revision_points` rejects 0.5/2.9/3.0/3.1/-1.1/-2.9/-3.0/-3.1/bool/numeric-strings and accepts -3/-1/0/1/3; `_finite_int` strict; engine-level reproduction of the exact Codex probe (2.9/3.1/-1.1 → 50.0, `neutral_fallback`, `realized=[]`) + int-3 positive control (→ 65.0, realized). **Verify**: focused 63 OK; full offline `*us_short*` 2728 OK; doc-route guards 52 OK; py_compile OK; `git diff --check` CRLF-only; direct probe (2.9/3.1/-1.1/3.0/-3.0) all REJECTED → neutral, not scored. No provider/live/network, Pass2, R3 seam, DataHub, production/ship-gate, A-share crossing, or threshold recalibration.
- **Codex closure (2026-06-30; PASS; OFFLINE)**: independently re-read the current scope and verified `_finite_int` is the only path for `analyst_revision_net`; direct probe rejected `0.5`, `2.9`, `3.0`, `3.1`, `-1.1`, `-2.9`, `-3.0`, `-3.1`, `True`, and `"3"` as non-scoring neutral fallback with `realized=[]`, while legal integers `3`, `1`, `0`, `-1`, and `-3` still scored as designed. Focused catalyst/schema tests 63 OK; full offline `*us_short*` 2728 OK; doc-route guards 52 OK; `py_compile` OK; `git diff --check` warning-only CRLF. No provider/live/network, Pass2, R3 seam, DataHub, production/ship-gate, A-share, A-long, US-long, or threshold recalibration was reviewed or changed.

### R-USSHORT-BATCH4-OFFLINE-ARTIFACT-MODE-PROVENANCE-GAP - offline fixture outputs are indistinguishable from operational weekly artifacts

- **Status**: resolved in reviewed working tree (Codex re-review PASS 2026-06-29; OFFLINE). The official action-table persister requires the exact immutable `run_origin` before any file is created, so a provenance-stripped record cannot be persisted as an unlabeled actionable CSV.
- **Severity**: P1 (official-output honesty / provenance; blocks treating batch4 artifacts as actionable weekly advice, but does not block the synthetic offline engineering run itself).
- **Scope reviewed**: US-short batch4 only: `runners/us_short_weekend_batch4.py`, `engine/us_short_weekend_orchestrator.py`, `engine/us_short_weekend_machine_record.py`, `engine/us_short_weekend_report.py`, `engine/us_short_weekend_private_write.py`, weekly renderer/contracts, context packet schema/examples/builder, and their offline tests. Batch5/provider/live/DataHub/Skill/production/A-share/US-long were excluded.
- **Technical evidence**: the supported runner defaults to `run_mode="offline_test"` (`runners/us_short_weekend_batch4.py:187-220`) and the orchestrator knows that mode, but it calls `assemble_machine_record(..., as_of=decision_date)`, `build_weekly_report(...)`, and `write_run_private(...)` without threading any mode/data-origin fact (`engine/us_short_weekend_orchestrator.py:256-273`). `build_weekly_report` section 1 reports only date/counts, section 11 renders injected provider health as “结构化、权威”, and section 13 declares no unclean item solely from coverage/no-dangling (`engine/us_short_weekend_report.py:321-350`); neither the machine record nor report carries `run_mode=offline_test` / `data_origin=caller_supplied_fixture`. Independent private-temp repro using the supported runner returned `emitted=True`, `report_has_offline_test=False`, `report_has_fixture=False`, and `machine_has_run_mode=False`; the generated report stated `provider_health=clean（结构化、权威）` and `本周无不 clean 项`. The caller can obtain that “clean” line by injecting the example's `fmp=ok/sec_edgar=ok` despite no provider call occurring.
- **Impact**: a synthetic/offline fixture report is written under the same official `runs_private/<decision_date>` and `weekly_private/<decision_date>` locations as future operational output and can be mistaken for a real weekly selection/advice artifact. The paper-only live-permission cell limits sizing but does not disclose that all market/provider facts were caller-supplied fixtures. This is a design/output-provenance gap and a code wiring bug; green validators currently certify the misleading surface.
- **Required repair**: define one immutable execution/data-origin fact at the runner/orchestrator boundary (at minimum `run_mode=offline_test`, `data_origin=caller_supplied_fixture`, `operational_use=not_authorized`); thread and reconcile it through the official machine record and weekly report; show an always-visible offline/fixture banner and include the offline limitation in “本周不 clean 项” (or an equivalent non-operational status). An offline run must not describe fixture-declared provider health as operationally “权威 clean”. Private write must reject a machine/report mode mismatch. Keep live hard-gated and do not add provider calls or batch5 work.
- **Closure tests**: add empty and nonempty supported-runner tests proving the machine artifact and rendered report both carry matching offline/fixture provenance; mutate/remove/swap mode provenance and require fail-closed/no-write; prove the report cannot emit the existing “provider 权威 clean + 本周无不 clean” combination in offline mode; retain out-of-window no-emit, private path, no-dangling, same-run reconciliation, and live-gate tests. Rerun focused batch4, all offline `test_us_short_*.py`, US-short schema tests, route-doc guards, `py_compile`, and `git diff --check`.
- **Repair (Claude 2026-06-29; OFFLINE; fixed pending Codex)**: defined the ONE immutable execution/data-origin fact in a single source `engine/us_short_run_origin.py` — `OFFLINE_TEST_RUN_ORIGIN = {run_mode: offline_test, data_origin: caller_supplied_fixture, operational_use: not_authorized}` + `validate_run_origin` (closed-world exact match) + `run_origin_for_mode` (only `offline_test` reaches the official chain; live is hard-gated upstream) + the stable `OFFLINE_DISCLOSURE_SENTINEL` and `offline_disclosure_lines`. **Threaded + reconciled**: the orchestrator derives `run_origin = run_origin_for_mode(run_mode)` and passes it to K/m2/N; `assemble_machine_record(..., run_origin)` stamps + validates it on the record (top-level `run_origin`), and `flatten_machine_record` preserves it onto the written machine artifact. `schemas/us_short_machine_record_contract.schema.json` adds `run_origin` const-pinned to the offline fact (optional only to keep pre-existing hand-built test records valid; the assembler always populates it, so a swapped value fails the schema). **Report**: `build_weekly_report(..., run_origin)` renders the always-visible offline disclosure as the FIRST lines of §1, makes §11 provider health read “离线 fixture 自报；offline_test 不认定运营级权威 clean，非真实 provider 调用” (never operationally 权威 clean), and §13 ALWAYS leads with the offline non-operational limitation (so it can never render “本周无不 clean 项”); `report_data` carries `run_origin`. **Private write**: `write_run_private(..., run_origin)` reconciles the machine record's `run_origin` against the passed fact AND requires the offline sentinel in the rendered report — a machine/report mode mismatch fails closed with NO write (runs after the flatten/§10 gate so a malformed record still surfaces its own typed error first). - **Codex slice-1a review FAIL (2026-06-30; `R-USSHORT-BATCH5-STATUS-RECORD-ROW-BINDING-GAP`)**: the new offline status-source layer is not ready to close R1 remainder (a). **Scope reviewed**: `engine/us_short_status_source.py`, `tests/provider/test_us_short_status_source.py`, `schemas/us_short_batch5_status_source_access_packet.schema.json`, `docs/us_short_batch5_status_source_access_packet_20260630.json`, and the adjacent `cheap_eligible` row-consumer boundary. This did not review or run provider/live status calls, `runners/us_short_universe_fetch.py` rewiring, candidate-artifact status-provenance schema expansion, R3 seam, DataHub, production, broker/order automation, A-share, A-long, or US-long. **Technical finding**: `status_flags_for_row(record)` validates only the status-record shape and then returns bare `row_flags` detached from `record["ticker"]`; it has no row-ticker parameter or identity check. Direct probe resolved a clean AAPL status record, extracted `{'delisted': False, 'halted': False, 'bankruptcy': False, 'otc': False}`, merged those flags into a separate DEAD row, and `cheap_eligible` returned `{'ticker': 'DEAD', 'eligible': True, 'reasons': []}` even though the same reference payload marked DEAD inactive/delisted. Same-class provenance probe mutated a resolved record to top-level `ticker='000001.SZ'`, `flags.delisted.as_of='1900-01-01'`, and `flags.delisted.coverage='nonsense'`; `validate_status_record` still returned `True` and `status_flags_for_row` still emitted all-clean row flags. The existing focused tests pass because they cover minimal/missing/wrong-source/bankruptcy-None shape mutants, but not record-to-row identity binding, canonical ticker validation, per-flag `as_of`/`observed_at` equality, coverage enums, or source-specific provenance semantics. **Why material**: this layer is explicitly intended to convert real per-ticker status-source observations into the `cheap_eligible` row contract before the runner removes its hardwired `False` status flags. If the API can detach a clean status record from its ticker, a caller/seam bug or forged intermediate record can turn "real status checked" into another hardwired-clean path for a different ticker, reintroducing the R1 fail-open class before live integration exists. The blast radius is bounded today because the runner is not rewired and live fetch is still gated, but the offline integration surface would be unsafe to consume as-is. **Required repair**: bind status records to rows at the conversion boundary and harden record validation. A safe shape is `status_flags_for_row(record, *, row_ticker)` or equivalent, requiring canonical `record["ticker"] == canonical_us_ticker(row_ticker)` before any flags are emitted; noncanonical record tickers must be rejected by `validate_status_record`; each flag's provenance `as_of`/`observed_at` must match the top-level record, and `coverage` / source-specific provenance values must be closed-world validated according to the resolver's emitted states. Add adversarial tests for AAPL-clean-record applied to DEAD row rejected/no flags, noncanonical top-level ticker rejected, mismatched per-flag as_of/observed_at rejected, invalid coverage rejected, and the positive same-ticker clean/delisted/halted/bankruptcy paths. - **Required repair**: freeze a minimum-coverage policy — the primary score requires the same feature set / minimum coverage; missing features are neutral or restricted per governance, never auto-full-weight on the remainder. The Codex probe (single-feature `SHORT=999` outranking `FULL`) now puts SHORT in `insufficient_coverage` (not scored); a partial-but-extreme ticker at min-coverage is pulled toward neutral and cannot outrank a genuinely full-feature top. ### R-USSHORT-BATCH4-SELECTION-TRACE-AND-RECALL-CLOSURE-GAP - Top15 selection identity is lost/recomputed and catalyst recall bypasses the universe eligibility gate

- **Status**: resolved (Codex user-authorized fix + scoped self-check PASS 2026-06-28; canonical selection record now reconciles through report Top15 including `holding_in_top15`).
- **Severity**: P1 (selection correctness and same-run traceability; blocks trusting Top15 identity/order or build-capacity priority).
- **Scope reviewed**: `engine/us_short_eligibility_gate.py`, `engine/us_short_weekend_pipeline.py`, `engine/us_short_weekend_analysis.py`, `engine/us_short_weekend_basket.py`, `engine/us_short_weekend_orchestrator.py`, `engine/us_short_weekend_report.py`, and corresponding tests.
- **Technical finding**: `_select_top15` produces `selection_details` with `selection_bucket`, selection-time core/theme scores, and `selection_rank`, but the orchestrator passes only ticker-keyed analysis payloads downstream. `analyze_rows` recomputes a separate core score and drops the selection metadata; `resolve_build_capacity` then creates a new `selection_rank` by sorting surviving builds on that recomputed core score only. There is no same-run equality/reconciliation between selection scores and analysis scores. A direct two-name probe selected `AAA` rank 1 (`core=100`) and `BBB` rank 2 (`core=0`), injected analysis scores in reverse, and emitted machine rows with `AAA` rank 2 / `BBB` rank 1. `selection_bucket` never reaches the machine/action table, and report §7 prints `action_rank` as the Top15 rank. In the same selection boundary, `inject_catalyst_recall` appends any syntactically valid ticker without requiring it to exist in the universe or pass `cheap_eligible`; a direct probe with universe `[AAPL]` admitted recall-only `PENNY` ahead of AAPL.
- **Impact**: the system can say one list was selected, allocate scarce weekly build/cash priority using a different ranking, and lose whether a name came from core/theme/overlap. Recall can also bypass the mandatory exchange/price/ADV/market-cap/status floor entirely.
- **Required repair**: establish one canonical per-ticker selection record and carry it through analysis, basket, machine record, action table, and report. Preserve `selection_rank` / `selection_bucket` / selection-time scores; either consume the same score object downstream or fail closed when recomputed analysis scores differ. Basket/cash/action ranking must use the preserved selection rank; report Top15 must display it, not `action_rank`. Catalyst recall must resolve against the same active universe row and pass the cheap eligibility gate (or be explicitly represented as recall-but-ineligible and excluded), never inject a ticker-only bypass. Add reversed-score, lost-bucket, report-rank, off-universe recall, below-floor recall, disqualifying-status recall, duplicate, and positive-control tests.
- **Plain language**: batch4 currently selects one ranking, silently builds another ranking later, and lets the recall lane add a stock that never passed the basic tradability gate.
- **Repair (Claude `修复` 2026-06-27, batch4 round-2 slice 2 — pending Codex review; OFFLINE only)**: one canonical selection identity threaded end-to-end. **(2a)** `run_weekend_pipeline._build_analysis_rows` attaches the `_select_top15` selection record (`selection_rank` / `selection_bucket` / selection-time core+theme scores) to each admitted row; it rides the `{**row}` chain into the §10 machine record. `us_short_weekend_analysis._analyze_one` carries it AND reconciles the selection-time vs the recomputed §4.2 core_score (when both present): a divergence > 1e-6 fails CLOSED (one core_score per run) — the review's reversed-score probe now raises instead of emitting a reversed rank. **(2b)** `us_short_weekend_basket.resolve_build_capacity` now orders/ranks builds by the PRESERVED `selection_record.selection_rank` (asc), NOT a re-derived analysis core_score; the weekly-limit uses the survivor position while the EMITTED selection_rank is the (possibly sparse) preserved Top15 rank; cash allocation already consumes that rank; `us_short_weekend_report` §7 Top15 now displays the preserved `selection_rank` + selection-time core_score, not `action_rank`. Orphaned `_finite_number` + `import math` removed from the basket. **(2c)** `us_short_eligibility_gate.inject_catalyst_recall` takes a `universe_eligibility` {ticker: cheap_eligible bool} map and admits a recalled name ONLY if it is an active universe row passing the §4.0 floor (exchange/price/ADV/market-cap/status); an off-universe / below-floor recall is recorded `recall_excluded` (reason off_universe|below_floor) and never admitted; `run_selection` builds the map and surfaces `recall_excluded`. ### R-USSHORT-BATCH4-OFFICIAL-REPORT-SOURCE-BINDING-GAP - official report accepts contradictory free-text gate claims and detached coverage/exclusion facts

- **Status**: resolved in reviewed working tree (Codex re-review PASS 2026-06-29; OFFLINE). Lifecycle count, run identity, and §12 due-item/upgrade detail are bound to the independently validated lifecycle stage result at private persistence.
- **Severity**: P0 (official-output honesty and ship-gate boundary; a weekly report can claim healthy/full-size/fully-covered states that the machine run did not establish).
- **Scope reviewed**: `engine/us_short_weekend_report.py`, `engine/us_short_coverage_honesty.py`, `engine/us_short_exclusion_summary.py`, `engine/us_short_weekend_orchestrator.py`, `engine/us_short_provider_health.py`, `engine/us_short_ship_gate_sizing.py`, action-table projection, and report/orchestrator tests.
- **Technical finding**: the report correctly reconciles dates, lifecycle readiness, and hot-excluded count, but the remaining boundary-bearing facts are caller prose or detached lists. `account_risk_note`, `theme_opportunity_state`, `provider_health_note`, and `ship_gate_note` accept any nonblank text and are not reconciled to basket/regime/provider/evidence outputs. An end-to-end probe produced `final_action=观察 / risk_cooldown` from `portfolio_guard_status=cooldown` while the report said `portfolio_guard=normal`, displayed a contradictory theme state, `all providers clean`, and `full_size_eligible`. `coverage_inputs` has no ticker identity or exact row-set reconciliation; a report containing one real holding accepted `coverage_inputs=[]`, rendered `本周持仓覆盖 0 行 ... 无覆盖缺口（全 full）`, then claimed `本周无不 clean 项`. `exclusion_data` is injected independently and is not derived/reconciled against Pass1/Pass2 reject outcomes, which the selection stage does not retain. Coverage, portfolio guard, symbol cooldown, and live-permission cells consequently remain empty in the official action table even when those facts changed the decision.
- **Impact**: the user-facing report can contradict the action engine and overstate source health, holding coverage, ship-gate permission, or exclusion completeness. The arbitrary `full_size_eligible` banner is a direct bypass of the design's live-normalized AND gate.

Add contradiction probes for every sibling surface, empty/missing/extra/duplicate coverage rows, zeroed exclusion summaries after real rejects, paper-only/full-size spoofing, degraded provider health, and matching positive controls.

### R-USSHORT-BATCH4-ACTION-PRICE-MAPPING-GAP - action-table validation does not enforce the frozen final_action to price-field mapping

- **Status**: resolved (Codex strict re-review PASS 2026-06-28; action-keyed price requirements are enforced at machine assembly and action-table/private projection). Previously open (Codex strict full `US-short batch4` review FAIL 2026-06-27).
- **Repair (Claude 2026-06-28)**: SINGLE-SOURCE §9 action↔price matrix `ACTION_REQUIRED_PRICE_FIELDS` + `action_price_error()` in `engine/us_short_weekend_decision.py` (next to `action_reason_error`), covering ALL 9 frozen `final_action` incl. the v1-deferred 加仓/减仓/清仓-止盈 so a later activation cannot bypass the gate: 建仓/加仓→`limit_order_price`, 减仓→`take_profit_reduce_price`, 清仓-止损→`stop_clear_price`, 清仓-止盈→`take_profit_exit_price`, 清仓-事件→`event_clear_reference_price`, 持有/观察/否决-避开→N/A. Required price must be a finite POSITIVE number. Enforced ACTION-keyed (independent of `executable`/row-class) at (a) machine-record assembly `_validate_ranked_row` BEFORE §10-clean; (b) action_table `_validate_price_projection` BEFORE the §11.3 lift / executable early-return; (c) private persistence transitively via `flatten_machine_record`. Triangulation test: matrix keys == FINAL_ACTIONS, required fields ⊆ frozen §11.3 columns. Tests: per-action positive + missing/non-positive/non-finite/wrong-type reverse (every action) + event-clear closure rejected at BOTH assembly and flatten + positives. Full offline `*us_short*` 2496 OK; boundary 8 / doc guards 52.
- **Severity**: P1 (operation advice completeness; an actionable exit can be official while its required execution price is blank).
- **Scope reviewed**: `engine/us_short_weekend_decision.py`, `engine/us_short_weekend_machine_record.py`, `engine/us_short_no_dangling_validator.py`, `engine/us_short_weekend_action_table.py`, report/private-write paths, and tests.
- **Technical finding**: the decision engine maps a holding `position_hard_veto` to `清仓-事件`, but neither the machine/no-dangling gate nor `_validate_price_projection` requires `event_clear_reference_price` for that action. The holding projection only requires stop/status/engine. A direct probe assembled, flattened, and accepted a §10-clean official row with `final_action=清仓-事件` and `event_clear_reference_price=null`. The same validator structure is row-class-based, not action-based, so the complete 9-action mapping is not machine-enforced.
- **Impact**: the system can give an official clear/reduce/add/profit action without the corresponding executable/reference price, violating design §9's one-to-one action-price contract and weakening the stated purpose of reasonable, price-bearing operation advice.
- **Required repair**: add a single-source action-to-required-price matrix covering all frozen `final_action` values: build/add entry fields; reduce TP1; stop-clear stop; profit-clear TP2; event-clear event reference; and the explicit N/A rules for hold/observe/reject. Enforce it before machine clean, before action-table projection, and before private persistence without duplicating the mapping. Add one positive and missing/wrong-price reverse test for every action value, including currently deferred actions so later activation cannot bypass the gate.
- **Plain language**: a row can currently say “clear because of an event” while leaving the event-clear price blank, and the official validator still calls it clean.

Selection bucket was lost, while action-table `portfolio_guard_status`, `symbol_cooldown_status`, `coverage_status`, `coverage_gap_tags`, `live_permission_status`, and warning were blank.
- **Impact**: “§10 clean / no dangling” currently means only that the records provided are internally valid, not that all decision-driving fields were registered, traceable, and landed. Fields can silently disappear between a stage and official output.
- **Required repair**: define the complete expected batch4 field manifest by row/stage and make the machine assembler emit a registry disposition for every computed or consumed decision field. The validator must perform the reverse check: expected field absent, duplicate, wrong source/landing, or output field present without a registry record => not clean. Cover selection metadata, data/coverage status, provider health, portfolio guard, symbol cooldown, cash allocation, theme/macro inputs, live permission, and all action-driving traces. Add planted-deletion tests across every manifest member plus positive controls for legitimately N/A/shadow/dropped fields.
- **Plain language**: the no-dangling checker only checks the paperwork it receives; it does not notice missing paperwork. Important fields can vanish and the run still gets a clean stamp.

### R-USSHORT-BATCH5-UNIVERSE-FETCH-RAW-ROOT-SCOPE-BYPASS - universe fetch runner raw_root not validated against provider_samples/ prefix

- **Status**: resolved (self-review FAIL 2026-06-26 → self-repair → self-review PASS 2026-06-26; `_sv.validate_raw_root(raw_root)` called in `run_fetch` before any write; adversarial test `TestRawRootScopeGuard` added; 30 tests OK; 2368 full offline OK).
- **Severity**: P1 (US-short batch5 FMP universe fetch; raw FMP screener response — containing prices/volumes for thousands of stocks — can be written outside gitignored area if raw_root is injected via CLI or function arg pointing outside provider_samples/).
- **Scope reviewed**: `runners/us_short_fmp_universe_fetch.py`, `schemas/us_short_fmp_universe_fetch_authorization.schema.json`, `docs/us_short_fmp_universe_fetch_authorization_20260626.json`, `tests/provider/test_us_short_fmp_universe_fetch.py`.
- **Finding type**: code bug / private-output no-dangling / security boundary gap. Same class as `R-USSHORT-BATCH5-INCIDENT-WRITER-DUPLICATE-PARTIAL-WRITE` and the batch5 probe `_validate_raw_root` gap.
- **Technical finding**: `run_fetch`'s `raw_root` parameter is passed to `_write_json_atomic(screener_rows, raw_path)` without validating that `raw_root` resolves to a path under `ROOT / "provider_samples"`. The `_check_gitignore()` guard only verifies the `.gitignore` file contains the string `"provider_samples/"` — it does NOT verify the actual `raw_root` path is under that directory. A caller using `--raw-root /tmp/exposed/` passes the gitignore check while writing raw FMP screener payloads to an untracked, non-gitignored path; the summary then claims `raw_payload_root_gitignored: True` regardless. The existing `us_egs_sample_validation.validate_raw_root(raw_root)` (line 411 of `runners/us_egs_sample_validation.py`) already implements the exact required check: resolves raw_root and verifies it is under `ROOT / "provider_samples"`, raising `ValueError` otherwise.
- **Why material**: the raw FMP screener response contains market data (prices, volumes, market caps) for 1000-4000 NYSE/NASDAQ stocks. If written outside gitignored provider_samples/, it can be accidentally staged and committed to git, leaking bulk market data from a paid FMP API key and violating the privacy boundary of the authorization packet.
- **Required repair**: (1) Import `us_egs_sample_validation` in `runners/us_short_fmp_universe_fetch.py` and call `us_egs_sample_validation.validate_raw_root(raw_root)` in `run_fetch` immediately after `_check_gitignore()` and before any network call or file write. (2) Add an adversarial test that calls `run_fetch` (or `_validate_raw_root` once extracted) with `raw_root` pointing outside `provider_samples/` (e.g., a temp dir) and verifies `ValueError` is raised before any file is written. Keep all existing tests passing. No live FMP call, no provider/network, no DataHub, no production path during repair.
- **Tests expected**: existing 28 tests must remain OK; new adversarial test for raw_root escape; full offline `*us_short*` regression; doc/route guards; `git diff --check`; `git status --short`.
- **Plain language**: the runner checks that .gitignore contains "provider_samples/" but never checks whether the actual output path IS under provider_samples/. Passing a different path bypasses the whole privacy guard while the summary still claims the raw data is gitignored.
- **Carry-forward (2026-06-27)**: the FMP and IBKR universe runners were superseded by `runners/us_short_universe_fetch.py` (Massive+SEC). The `_sv.validate_raw_root(raw_root)` guard + the raw-root-escape adversarial test (`TestGuards.test_raw_root_escape_rejected`) carry forward into the new runner/`tests/provider/test_us_short_universe_fetch.py`, so the fix remains in force on the live data path.

### R-USSHORT-BATCH5-INCIDENT-WRITER-DUPLICATE-PARTIAL-WRITE - batch5 incident-log writer allows duplicate incident ids and can append before failing on corrupt existing log

- **Status**: resolved (Codex `review PASS` 2026-06-25; auto-commit closeout).
- **Severity**: P1 (US-short batch5 offline private-output writer; blocks accepting / committing this writer slice before repair or any later incident-log runtime use).
- **Scope reviewed**: current dirty worktree after HEAD `34a9f8dc`; `engine/us_short_batch5_incident_log_writer.py`, `schemas/us_short_batch5_incident_log_record.schema.json`, `tests/provider/test_us_short_batch5_incident_log_writer.py`, `tests/schema/test_us_short_batch5_incident_log_record_schema.py`, `docs/README.md`, and top `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`. No provider/live/network/FMP/SEC/yfinance/Web/X/DataHub/production/raw call, provider status polling, fallback execution, raw-payload read/write, live_normalized claim, or ship-gate claim ran during review.
- **Finding type**: code bug / execution blocker / private-output no-dangling bug. Not a provider authorization blocker and not a design gap.
- **Technical finding**: the owner incident-log contract defines `incident_id` as a stable unique incident identifier, but `engine/us_short_batch5_incident_log_writer.py::write_incident_record` appends a validated row without checking existing `incident_id` values. A Codex local private-temp probe wrote the same valid record twice and the writer accepted it (`duplicate_result = accepted_duplicate`, `duplicate_lines = 2`). The same function also writes the new JSONL line before reading and validating the existing log: it creates the target dir and appends at lines 261-266, then calls `_load_jsonl(log_path)` at line 268. A second Codex probe pre-created `incident_log.jsonl` with malformed JSON; the writer raised `IncidentLogWriterError: invalid existing incident_log.jsonl line 1`, but only after appending the new row (`corrupt_lines_after = 2`), leaving a private log mutation without a refreshed summary.
- **Why material**: batch5 incident logging is supposed to be the private evidence-traceback surface for later provider/fallback incidents. Duplicate ids break stable incident identity, and append-before-preflight can leave a dangling / desynchronized private log and summary. That weakens no-dangling / evidence-traceback guarantees before any later reviewed incident writer, fallback, provider/live, DataHub/runner, production storage, live_normalized, or ship-gate boundary.
- **Required repair**: pre-read and validate any existing JSONL before creating or appending a new record; reject malformed existing logs with no file mutation; enforce unique `incident_id` across existing records plus the new record; then write the append and summary only after all preflight checks pass. Add adversarial tests for duplicate `incident_id`, corrupt existing JSONL no-mutation, and summary/log synchronization. Keep the writer offline-only and preserve all no-provider-live / no-status-polling / no-fallback-execution / no-DataHub / no-production / no-live_normalized / no-ship-gate locks.
- **Tests expected**: target `tests.provider.test_us_short_batch5_incident_log_writer` and `tests.schema.test_us_short_batch5_incident_log_record_schema`; full batch5 target suites; route/doc guards; `tests/provider`; full offline `*us_short*`; `py_compile`; direct duplicate-id and corrupt-existing-log probes; `git diff --check`; `git status --short --untracked-files=all`. Do not run provider/live/network/FMP/SEC/yfinance/Web/X/DataHub/production/raw calls while repairing.

Existing malformed JSONL now raises before any new row or summary is written. `tests/provider/test_us_short_batch5_incident_log_writer.py` adds adversarial tests for duplicate-id no-mutation and corrupt-existing-log no-mutation / no-summary behavior. Keep the current conservative no-promotion behavior unless the design is explicitly changed.
- **Tests expected**: add adversarial tests for unknown `final_action`, lowercase / whitespace tickers in build and non-build paths, duplicate canonical identities, missing/invalid build sizing payload, stale/missing/non-canonical `per_ticker` keys, whitespace theme variants that would bypass SAME_THEME_WEEK_CAP, and positive controls for valid weekly-limit cap, valid same-theme cap, no-promotion, valid non-build carry-through, and selection_rank ordering. Keep target basket tests, adjacent pure US-short weekend suites, doc/route/README guards, `py_compile`, and `git diff --check` green.

### R-USSHORT-BATCH4-WEEKEND-SIZING-INPUT-CONTRACT-GAP - sizing stage can size duplicate / invalid build rows and accepts stale / non-canonical ticker inputs

- **Status**: resolved (Codex re-`审查 PASS` 2026-06-24).
- **Severity**: P1 (US-short batch4 slice 4d-ii-c per-row sizing / injected decision-result and sizing-context consumer validation; blocks accepting this sizing slice before 4d-ii-d build-limit / theme / cash / action-rank integration, machine-record / no-dangling assembly, private output, provider/live wiring, DataHub, or production-like use).
- **Scope reviewed**: current uncommitted US-short batch4 slice 4d-ii-c after HEAD `8205ebe4`; modified `docs/README.md`, modified `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`, and untracked `engine/us_short_weekend_sizing.py`, `tests/test_us_short_weekend_sizing.py`. Read authority from `AGENTS.md`, `docs/README.md`, `docs/CURRENT.md`, this Hot Queue, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md` top entries, `docs/AI_REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md`, `docs/us_short_system_design.md` sections 6 / 7 / 8 / 9 / 10 / 11 / 12 / 18.1 / 18.2, `docs/pre_codex_self_review_checklist.md`, and the current US-short batch4 implementation/tests. No provider/live/network/DataHub/Skill/production/broker/order/A-share/US-long path was run.
- **Detected by**: Codex `审查`, 2026-06-24.
- **Technical finding**: `engine/us_short_weekend_sizing.py::size_rows` validates only broad row shape (`final_action` is a string, `ticker` is a string, `price.action_fields` is a dict) before sizing or carrying rows forward. It does not validate the decision-row value contract or exact sizing-context coverage. Direct probes show: (1) two duplicate provisional build rows for `AAPL` are both accepted and each sized to 98 shares, so the aggregate same-ticker model size becomes 196 shares while the advertised single-ticker cap for the row is 98 shares; (2) a malformed build row with `price.executable=False` but valid `valid_entry_high` / `stop_clear_price` is still sized to 98 shares instead of failing closed or degrading; (3) an unknown `final_action="BANANA"` is carried forward with `sizing=None`, leaving an invalid action vocab value for downstream consumers; and (4) `sizing_context.per_ticker` accepts an unused stale key such as `STALE` even though the slice handoff claims per-ticker closed-world validation and prior batch4 injected-data consumers now reject stale/extra keys.
- **Why material**: slice 4d-ii-c is the first stage that turns provisional `建仓` rows into concrete model share counts and claims to enforce the §8 single-ticker cap plus fail-closed injected sizing context. If duplicate ticker rows are accepted, the same security can bypass the cap by appearing twice; if non-executable build rows or unknown action vocab are carried forward, 4d-ii-d, §10 machine-record/no-dangling, renderer, and private output may receive valid-looking size/action payloads that contradict the decision contract. This is the same consumer-validation class already caught in earlier batch4 slices: malformed or stale injected data must not masquerade as clean operational output.
- **Required repair**: validate the 4d-ii-b decision-result contract at the `size_rows` boundary before sizing or carry-through. At minimum: require `final_action` to be a known frozen action vocab value (or the exact 4d-ii-b output subset); for `建仓`, require candidate-compatible row identity and `price.executable is True` with valid build price levels; reject duplicate ticker identities that would let same-ticker rows bypass per-ticker caps (prefer canonical unique rowset validation, at least unique build tickers); require `sizing_context.per_ticker` to exactly cover the build ticker set with no missing or stale/extra keys, and validate those keys as strings under the same canonical US ticker policy used upstream; keep current valid sizing math intact (`risk_based_base_shares` × `position_cap` × harshest discount × min(single-ticker/liquidity caps), below-min → `观察(cost_inefficient_min_size)`). Preserve valid non-build carry-through only after the action vocab / row identity is valid.
- **Tests expected**: extend `tests/test_us_short_weekend_sizing.py` with adversarial cases for duplicate build ticker rows, stale/extra `per_ticker` keys, unknown `final_action`, build rows with `price.executable=False`, build rows with incompatible row context, and positive controls for a unique valid build, valid non-build carry-through, missing build sizing input fail-closed, single-ticker cap binding, liquidity cap binding, harshest discount, and below-min observe. Keep target sizing tests, adjacent weekend decision / analysis / position sizing / regime / price / eligibility tests, doc/route/README guards, and `py_compile` green.
- **Boundary**: repair only `engine/us_short_weekend_sizing.py`, `tests/test_us_short_weekend_sizing.py`, directly necessary README/docstring wording if the public contract changes, and closeout docs. Do not start 4d-ii-d build-limit / same-theme / theme_probe cost floor / cash allocation / action-rank, machine-record/no-dangling assembly, renderer/private-output, provider/live calls, DataHub, Skill, production, broker/order, A-share, or US-long work.

Direct probes reproduced duplicate `AAPL` builds each sized to 98 shares, non-executable build price sized to 98 shares, unknown final action carried through, and stale extra `per_ticker` input accepted. ### R-USSHORT-BATCH4-WEEKEND-PIPELINE-DATACONTEXT-VALIDATION-GAP - selection front can default missing Pass2 signals clean and emit raw holding tickers

- **Status**: resolved (Codex re-`审查 PASS` 2026-06-24).
- **Severity**: P1 (US-short batch4 slice 4d-i data_context consumer-validation / candidate and holding identity; blocks accepting this pipeline slice before 4d-ii output/machine-record wiring, provider/live wiring, DataHub, or production-like use).
- **Scope reviewed**: current uncommitted US-short batch4 slice 4d-i after HEAD `18bc0e92`; modified `docs/README.md`, modified `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`; untracked `engine/us_short_weekend_pipeline.py` and `tests/test_us_short_weekend_pipeline.py`. Read authority from `AGENTS.md`, `docs/README.md`, `docs/CURRENT.md`, this Hot Queue, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md` top entries, `docs/AI_REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md`, `docs/us_short_system_design.md` sections 2 / 2.1 / 3 / 4 / 10 / 11 / 12 / 18.0-18.2, `docs/pre_codex_self_review_checklist.md`, and the current US-short batch4 implementation/tests. No provider/live/network/DataHub/Skill/production/broker/order/A-share/US-long path was run.
- **Detected by**: Codex `审查`, 2026-06-24.
- **Technical finding**: `engine/us_short_weekend_pipeline.py::_validate_data_context` only checks `candidate_pass2_signals` is a dict and only checks holding tickers are non-empty strings. In `run_selection`, candidates are evaluated with `signals_by_ticker.get(t, {})`, so a missing Pass2 row, a miscased Pass2 key, or a recall-added candidate with no Pass2 record is treated as a clean signal payload. Direct probes show: `candidate_pass2_signals={}` admits `AAPL`; `{"aapl": {"delisted": True}}` still admits canonical `AAPL`; recall feed `["MSFT"]` with no `MSFT` Pass2 record admits `MSFT`; and extra stale Pass2 key `ZZZZ` is ignored. The holding side then emits `h["ticker"]` unchanged after `pass2_safety_admit(h["signals"], row_context="holding")`; probes show `000001.SZ`, `" aapl "`, and both `AAPL` plus `" aapl "` are accepted and emitted as holdings.
- **Why material**: slice 4d-i is the first batch4 stage that consumes the injected `data_context` and merges Pass1, catalyst recall, Pass2, and forced holdings into a downstream selection artifact. `docs/us_short_system_design.md` treats Pass2 as an audit-safety gate and requires the pipeline to thread canonical identities / consumer-validation before output assembly. A missing or miscased Pass2 signal row should not silently become "clean"; otherwise the safety gate can be bypassed by omission or key drift. Raw holding tickers create a second identity policy after 4c fixed candidate canonicality, so the same stock can appear under multiple spellings and even A-share-like codes can be carried into the US-short holding path before 4d-ii machine records / no-dangling / render consume it.
- **Required repair**: validate the per-candidate Pass2 signal map against the final canonical `candidates` list after catalyst recall. Use the same US ticker canonicality policy as 4c for `candidate_pass2_signals` keys; reject invalid keys and post-canonical duplicates; require exact canonical coverage for the final candidate set, including recall-added tickers, and fail closed on missing or stale extra keys. Stop using `.get(t, {})` as the default-clean path; each candidate must consume a present dict payload. Also canonicalize/validate holding tickers with the same policy before Pass2 output, reject blank / malformed / A-share-like codes and post-canonical duplicate holdings, and emit only canonical holding tickers. Keep out-of-window no-emit behavior unchanged, and do not start 4d-ii output/machine-record/render, provider/live, DataHub, Skill, A-share, or US-long work.
- **Tests expected**: extend `tests/test_us_short_weekend_pipeline.py` with adversarial cases for missing candidate Pass2 signals, miscased Pass2 key carrying a veto, recall-added candidate missing Pass2 signals, stale extra Pass2 key, non-dict Pass2 payload, lowercase/whitespace holding ticker canonicalization or rejection per chosen policy, A-share-like holding ticker rejection, duplicate holding identity rejection after canonicalization, and class-share positive controls (`BRK.B` / `BRK-A`). Existing happy path, out-of-window no-emit, feed=None no-fabrication, candidate entry-hard-veto exclusion, holding forced-in veto surfaced, and decision-date threading tests must remain green.
- **Boundary**: repair only `engine/us_short_weekend_pipeline.py`, `tests/test_us_short_weekend_pipeline.py`, directly necessary README/docstring wording if the public contract changes, and closeout docs. Do not modify 4a resolver / 4c gate behavior unless exposing an already-existing canonical helper is the narrowest way to avoid duplicate policy. Do not fetch data, run provider/live calls, start DataHub/Skill/production, touch A-share/US-long, or commit.

Direct probes reproduced the gaps above. `git status --short --untracked-files=all` showed modified `docs/README.md`, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`, and untracked pipeline module/test; `git log -8 --oneline` started at `18bc0e92`. No provider/live/network/DataHub/Skill/production/broker/order/A-share/US-long path was run.
- **Plain language**: the pipeline says Pass2 is a safety check, but if a candidate's Pass2 record is missing or spelled with the wrong case, the code treats it as clean and lets it in. Holdings also skip the ticker identity guard, so `aapl`, ` AAPL `, and even an A-share code can pass through this US-short path.

The implementation validates `cheap_eligible_tickers`, then sets `base = list(cheap_eligible_tickers)` and `seen = set(base)`, but returns `base + added`. The US-short design describes this as a candidate set / candidate names gate, not a row-multiset. Allowing a duplicate base ticker through while the slice claims de-dup can make one stock occupy multiple candidate slots, distort candidate counts and downstream Top15 capacity, and hide upstream duplicate-universe/provider rows. Because this boundary is where the future catalyst-recall feed is merged, the output must be a unique ticker candidate set or explicitly fail closed on duplicate input; silently preserving base duplicates is not the advertised contract.

- **Status**: resolved (Codex re-`审查 PASS` 2026-06-24).

No provider/live/network/DataHub/Skill/production/broker/order/A-share/US-long path was run.
- **Detected by**: Codex `shencha`, 2026-06-24.
- **Technical finding**: `engine/us_short_eligibility_gate.py::cheap_eligible` iterates the governed `disqualifying_status_flags`, but uses `row.get(flag, False)` and therefore treats an absent `delisted`, `halted`, `bankruptcy`, or `otc` field as a clean `False` status. Direct probes removed each flag one at a time and then all four flags; every case returned `{"eligible": True, "reasons": []}`. The current test suite locks this wrong behavior in `tests/test_us_short_eligibility_gate.py::test_status_absent_defaults_clean`, which asserts a row with no status flags remains eligible. Adjacent controls show the hole is specifically the missing-status case: present `True` flags reject, present non-bool flags reject, and missing numeric fields reject.
- **Why material**: the US-short design treats critical status unknowns conservatively. `docs/us_short_system_design.md` says key unknowns such as delisting / halt / bankruptcy / critical stock status block new buys or at least restrict, and Pass1 explicitly includes basic status in the cheap eligibility gate. Allowing a provider-mapped row that simply omits all status flags to pass as eligible lets "unknown status" masquerade as "confirmed clean" before Pass2. That can admit delisted/halted/bankruptcy/OTC-risk names into the candidate set while all current tests remain green.
- **Required repair**: make each governed status flag required at predicate-consumption time, unless Claude first changes the owner design with a reviewed narrower contract. The expected narrow repair is: for every flag in `governance["disqualifying_status_flags"]`, absent key -> explicit `status_<flag>_unknown_or_invalid` reason and `eligible=False`; present `True` -> existing `status_<flag>` reason; present non-bool -> existing invalid reason; present `False` -> clean. Replace `test_status_absent_defaults_clean` with adversarial tests for each missing flag and all-status-missing rejection, while preserving positive controls where all four flags are explicitly `False`.
- **Tests expected**: targeted `tests.test_us_short_eligibility_gate` must fail on missing `delisted` / `halted` / `bankruptcy` / `otc` / all-status flags and still pass fully eligible, at-floor, true-status, non-bool-status, numeric-missing, and multi-reason cases. `py_compile`, doc/route/README guards, and `git diff --check` must remain clean aside from existing CRLF warnings. Do not start 4c-ii-b Pass2/catalyst work, 4d orchestration, provider/live calls, DataHub, Skill, production, broker/order, A-share, or US-long work.

Independent probe results: missing `delisted`, `halted`, `bankruptcy`, `otc`, or all four status flags all returned eligible with no reasons; present non-bool status values returned invalid reasons; missing `price`, `adv_usd`, and `market_cap_usd` returned invalid reasons. - **Resolution** (Claude `修复` 2026-06-24, working tree; 用户 `修复` 即授权): valid + in-scope — and I had locked the bug in my own test. `cheap_eligible` used `row.get(flag, False)`, defaulting an ABSENT critical status flag to clean, and `test_status_absent_defaults_clean` asserted that fail-open as correct. ### R-USSHORT-BATCH4-ELIGIBILITY-GOVERNANCE-SEMANTIC-PIN-GAP - eligibility governance schema accepts semantic drift in Pass1 gate constants

- **Status**: resolved (Codex re-`审查 PASS` 2026-06-24).

Authority checked from `AGENTS.md`, `docs/README.md`, `docs/CURRENT.md`, this Hot Queue, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md` top entries, `docs/AI_REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md`, `docs/us_short_system_design.md` sections 2.1 / 3 / 4 / 5 / 11 / 12 / 18.0-18.2, and `docs/pre_codex_self_review_checklist.md`. No provider/live/network/DataHub/Skill/production/broker/order/A-share/US-long path was run.
- **Detected by**: Codex `shencha`, 2026-06-24.
- **Technical finding**: the new schema is closed-world for object shape, but it does not pin the governed semantics that the preset and route row claim are frozen for this slice. In `schemas/us_short_eligibility_governance.schema.json`, `exchange_whitelist` is only `minItems: 1` with arbitrary non-empty string items (lines 19-21), so `["OTC"]`, `["NYSE American"]`, `["NYSE"]`, or any other non-empty string set would satisfy the schema even though the preset and notes define canonical NYSE/NASDAQ and say extension requires reviewed governance change. `disqualifying_status_flags` is only a non-empty unique subset of the allowed enum (lines 33-35), so dropping `halted`, `bankruptcy`, or `otc` still satisfies the schema; the test only rejects an unknown flag, not missing required disqualifiers (`tests/schema/test_us_short_eligibility_governance_schema.py` lines 70-71). The three Sec. 13.1 anchor fields are only positive integers (schema lines 37-39), so changing or swapping `2`, `19`, and `21` would validate; the test only rejects a string type (test lines 73-74), not a wrong numeric anchor. The threshold floors are likewise only positive numbers (schema lines 28-30; test lines 37-41 / 64-65), so weakening the initial v1 gates from `$5 / $5M / $300M` to tiny positive values would still pass the schema and test. ### R-USSHORT-BATCH4-CANONICAL-ASOF-CALENDAR-CONTRACT-GAP - canonical resolver accepts impossible dates, duplicate session rows, and non-RTH scope

- **Status**: resolved@`c8e9097` (Codex re-`审查 PASS` 2026-06-24).
- **Severity**: P1 (canonical decision-window integrity; blocks accepting US-short batch4 slice 4a before any pipeline wiring or forward-evidence use).
