RESOLVED P1 (2026-06-21): US-short two-axis regime governance schema under-pins §7 input-axis and safety mechanics. status `resolved`(working tree; 用户 `修复` 即授权; status `resolved` until Codex re-`审查 PASS` + 用户 `提交`); Required ID `R-USSHORT-REGIME-GOVERNANCE-INPUT-AXES-UNDERPINNED`; severity `P1` (schema-contract / future batch-2 regime+sizing consumer / provider-gate safety before any engine consumes the governance artifact). Scope reviewed: current dirty US-short §7 regime governance slice, including `schemas/us_short_regime_governance.schema.json`, `presets/us_short_regime_governance_20260620.json`, `tests/schema/test_us_short_regime_governance_schema.py`, `docs/README.md`, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`, `docs/system_risk_register.md`, and `docs/us_short_system_design.md` §7/§8/§13.

Finding (`R-USSHORT-REGIME-GOVERNANCE-INPUT-AXES-UNDERPINNED`): the preset and tests pin the four `market_risk_regime` caps, the high-level two-axis booleans, anti-chatter booleans, `unknown_defaults_defensive`, scope booleans, and `threshold_calibration_item_id=3`, but several design-locked §7 mechanics are still only prose in `description`/`notes` or absent from the schema/preset. Specifically, the schema has no const-pinned field for the risk-axis input set `VIX + SPY/QQQ + breadth`; no machine field proving QQQ is required in the market-trend axis; no field for `VIX 未授权 / unavailable` becoming an unknown axis with fallback to `SPY/QQQ + breadth` plus conservative unknown downgrade; no field that breadth comes from the base universe and does not depend on paid industry ETFs; no structured unknown-severity policy for `缺一项降级 / 缺关键项至少防御 / 严重 restricted`; and no const for the explicit upgrade confirmation rule `连续 2 次周跑更好或站回阈值上方缓冲`. Independent probe: the design §7 contains all of `必须含 QQQ`, `VIX 未授权 / unavailable`, `缺一项降级`, and `连续 2 次周跑`; the schema properties `risk_axis_inputs`, `vix_unavailable_policy`, `unknown_degradation_policy`, and `upgrade_confirmation_weekly_runs` are all absent; the preset does not mention `QQQ`, base-universe breadth, or `unapproved`. Existing tests pass because they only assert the current cap ladder and coarse booleans, not schema rejection for these same-class contract drifts.

Materiality: this is the same schema-contract class as the earlier US-short under-pinning findings: the current artifact is meant to freeze §7 before the batch-2 regime/position engine consumes it. If a future consumer trusts this schema, it can validate a governance artifact or implementation path that drops QQQ, uses only SPY, treats VIX provider-unavailable as clean/aggressive, depends on paid industry ETFs for breadth, upgrades after one good week, or weakens missing-input downgrades. That can change the market-risk cap and new-entry permission while still appearing schema-valid. The current slice has no executable engine yet, so this is not a runtime regression, but it is material before engine/provider/DataHub work.

Required repair: make the §7 governance schema reject the missing mechanics instead of leaving them as prose. Add negative schema tests requiring `jsonschema.ValidationError` for dropping QQQ, dropping breadth, changing VIX-unavailable to aggressive/clean, requiring paid industry ETF breadth, weakening unknown downgrade, and reducing upgrade confirmation to one week. Finding (`R-USSHORT-WEEKLY-REPORT-SCHEMA-UNDERPINNED`): the preset and tests currently match the design, but the schema does not actually freeze several governed constants that the slice claims to freeze. `sections` is only `minItems=maxItems=13` with string items, so a 13-item array with arbitrary or reordered section titles validates. `lifecycle_reminder_count_consistency` is only a non-empty string, so the "section 1 == section 12" invariant can be replaced by arbitrary text and still validates. `mandatory_banner.elements[*].tag` is only a non-empty string, so the machine-readable banner identities can drift while ids/count/always_shown still pass. Independent schema mutation probe results: `rename_section_same_count=ACCEPTED`, `reorder_sections_same_count=ACCEPTED`, `lifecycle_rule_drift=ACCEPTED`, and `banner_tag_drift=ACCEPTED`. Existing tests catch the committed preset's design faithfulness, but they do not require `jsonschema.ValidationError` for those same-count / same-shape schema drifts.

Materiality: this file is a batch-1 declarative output contract meant to freeze the §11.2 weekly_report surface before the batch-3 renderer and field_registry consumers exist. If a future renderer or registry gate trusts schema validation, it can accept a contract where "Top15 选股" or "字段·模块生命周期提醒" has been renamed/reordered, where lifecycle count consistency is no longer section 1 vs section 12, or where the price-clock banner id points to a different tag. That weakens the same no-dangling / honest-output guarantee this slice is supposed to establish, even though the current preset happens to be correct.

Required repair: make the schema reject governed weekly_report identity drift, not just the current preset tests. At minimum const-pin the full ordered 13-section array in `sections` (it is acceptable to generate that const mechanically from `docs/us_short_system_design.md`, but the tracked schema must validate the exact set/order), const-pin or structurally encode `lifecycle_reminder_count_consistency` so the rule cannot drift away from section 1 == section 12, and const-pin the five banner `tag` machine ids (`true_false_observe_split`, `macro_cluster_warning`, `ship_gate_progress`, `price_clock`, `hot_excluded_notice`) in their current order. Add negative schema tests requiring `jsonschema.ValidationError` for same-count section rename, same-count section reorder, lifecycle rule drift, and banner tag drift. Keep the design single-source test so schema consts stay byte-faithful to §11.2, and update README/SESSION_LOG wording if the schema-vs-test split changes. Boundary: weekly_report schema / preset / schema tests / README route row / this register only; do not implement renderer, field_registry, row-level no-dangling validator, batch-2 engine, provider calls, DataHub, broker/order automation, market fetch, paper/live evidence, or ship-gate changes.

Verify: action_table tests 21→26 OK; full discover 2916 OK (zero regression, +5 net); BOM=0; diff-check CLEAN. No provider/engine/fetch path.

Finding (`R-USSHORT-ACTION-TABLE-DESIGN-LOCKED-VOCAB-GAP`): the contract says it const-pins the §11.3 column set and all design-locked action_table vocabularies, but two action_table columns with explicit design vocabularies are left outside `design_locked_enums` and are even listed in `notes.deferred_vocab_columns`. `docs/us_short_system_design.md` §4.3 says `theme_source` values are `gics_established / provisional_discovered`; §8 says `macro_cluster_warning_level` values are `none / elevated / high`; §11.3 includes both columns in `action_table.csv`. Independent probe confirms both are core columns (`in_columns=True`) and both are not enum-pinned (`enum_pinned=False`). Existing tests still pass because `EXPECTED_ENUMS` hard-codes the incomplete 12-key set and does not assert these two design vocabularies.

Materiality: `theme_source` drives established-vs-provisional theme provenance and interacts with lifecycle / provisional-theme reporting, while `macro_cluster_warning_level=high` is designed to affect `risk_tags`, `action_confidence`, `model_position_size`, and the weekly report cluster banner. If future batch-2 row production or batch-3 validation trusts this contract, arbitrary values for these two columns can pass the shared contract while downstream aggregation / no-dangling / rendering logic assumes canonical tokens. That is the same contract-trust class this slice is meant to prevent before any consumer exists.

Required repair: add `theme_source` and `macro_cluster_warning_level` to `design_locked_enums` in schema and preset, const-pinned respectively to `["gics_established", "provisional_discovered"]` and `["none", "elevated", "high"]`. Remove both from the deferred-vocab note, update README/SESSION_LOG wording if needed, and add negative schema tests requiring `jsonschema.ValidationError` when either vocabulary drifts or is omitted. Keep positive cross-checks that these keys are real core columns. RESOLVED P1 (2026-06-20): US-short theme-lifecycle governance omits the design-required `cooling` holding decay tag / §9 re-evaluation path. status `resolved`(working tree; Codex re-`审查 PASS` 2026-06-20; pending 用户 `提交`); Required ID `R-USSHORT-THEME-LIFECYCLE-COOLING-HOLDING-EFFECT-GAP`; severity `P1` (schema-contract / future lifecycle classifier and report validator before batch 2/3 consumers exist). Scope reviewed: full current dirty-tree review of US-short batch 1 theme-lifecycle governance, including `schemas/us_short_theme_lifecycle_governance.schema.json`, `presets/us_short_theme_lifecycle_governance_20260620.json`, `tests/schema/test_us_short_theme_lifecycle_governance_schema.py`, `docs/README.md`, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`, and `docs/us_short_system_design.md` §4.3 / §10 / §11.3 / §13.1 #30 / §18.1 #14.

Finding (`R-USSHORT-THEME-LIFECYCLE-COOLING-HOLDING-EFFECT-GAP`): the design requires every degraded lifecycle state (`cooling`, `decayed`, and `retired`) to add a `theme_decay` tag to holdings and trigger §9 re-evaluation, while not mechanically clearing the holding. It also separately says `cooling` lowers holding `action_confidence`. The current governed action table const-pins `cooling.holding_effect = "action_confidence_down"` only; `decayed` and `retired` are the only states with `"theme_decay_tag_and_reeval"`. Independent probe confirms the schema-valid preset has `cooling` holding effect with no `theme_decay` and no `reeval`, while `decayed` / `retired` contain both. The tests do not catch the gap: `test_no_state_mechanically_clears_a_holding` comments "cooling/decayed/retired tag + re-evaluate" but only asserts `mechanical_clear == false`, and no test requires `cooling` to carry the tag / re-eval effect.

Materiality: `docs/us_short_system_design.md` §18.1 #14 says `theme_lifecycle_state` must affect seats / position / confidence / risk tags / observe reason and includes "持仓加 `theme_decay` 标 + §9 重评、不机械清仓". If a future lifecycle classifier or report validator trusts this governance artifact, a `cooling` theme can lower confidence without marking held names for the required decay review path. That weakens the no-dangling contract around `theme_lifecycle_state` and can let degraded themes avoid the review surface that the design explicitly requires before any batch 2/3 consumer exists.

Required repair: encode the full holding effect for `cooling`, not only the confidence effect. Acceptable repair shapes include splitting `holding_effect` into structured booleans / arrays (for example confidence_down + theme_decay_tag + section9_reeval + mechanical_clear=false) or const-pinning an unambiguous combined value for `cooling` that preserves both `action_confidence_down` and `theme_decay_tag_and_reeval`. Add tests that assert `cooling`, `decayed`, and `retired` all carry the theme-decay tag + §9 re-evaluation path, and that `cooling` still lowers confidence. Add negative schema tests requiring rejection when `cooling` loses either side of the combined holding effect. Update README wording if the field shape changes. Boundary: theme-lifecycle schema / preset / schema tests / README route row / this register only; do not implement the batch-2 lifecycle classifier, batch-3 validator/reporting, provider calls, DataHub, broker/order automation, market fetch, paper/live evidence, or ship-gate changes.

Resolution (Claude `修复` 2026-06-20, working tree; 用户 `修复` 即授权; status `resolved` until Codex re-`审查 PASS` + 用户 `提交`): judged valid and accepted — my single `holding_effect` enum collapsed the multi-dimensional holding effects, so `cooling` (which the design needs to BOTH lower action_confidence AND, like decayed/retired, add the theme_decay tag + trigger §9 re-eval) only carried `action_confidence_down`, dropping the design-required decay-review path (§18.1 #14 + §4.3 「cooling/decayed/retired 持仓加 theme_decay 标 + §9 重评、不机械清仓」). Same multi-member-coverage failure the just-strengthened checklist §A targets, here on the effect-DIMENSIONS × states matrix. Repair: replaced the `holding_effect` enum + top-level `mechanical_clear` with a structured `holding_effects` object const-pinned per state {action_confidence_down, theme_decay_tag, section9_reeval, mechanical_clear}. Now cooling = {confidence true, decay_tag true, reeval true, clear false}; decayed/retired = {confidence false, decay_tag true, reeval true, clear false}; provisional/confirmed = all false. Tests: `test_degraded_states_carry_theme_decay_tag_and_section9_reeval` (cooling/decayed/retired all tag+reeval; active none) + `test_only_cooling_lowers_confidence`; negative schema tests `test_schema_rejects_cooling_loses_theme_decay_tag` / `_section9_reeval` / `_confidence_down` (cooling losing either side of the combined effect is rejected) + the mechanical_clear mutation path updated; updated README to the structured shape. Verify: theme-lifecycle schema tests 21 OK; full discover `python -m unittest discover -s tests` 2890 OK (zero regression; +5 net); cooling holding_effects = confidence+decay_tag+reeval (no mechanical_clear), the cooling-drop mutations now rejected, real preset still validates; BOM/FFFD=0; `git diff --check` clean except CRLF; no provider/broker/fetch. Closure on Codex re-`审查 PASS` + 用户 `提交`.

Finding (`R-USSHORT-SCORING-PROFILE-SHADOW-WEIGHT-SCHEMA-GAP`): the prior four mutation cases are fixed, but `theme_plus` and `theme_aggressive` still use the generic `weightsShape` schema. Schema validation therefore accepts invalid shadow comparison weights. Independent probes: `theme_plus.weights={momentum:0.9, theme:0.9, catalyst:0.9}` validates successfully even though weights sum to 2.7; `theme_aggressive.weights={momentum:0.8, theme:0.1, catalyst:0.1}` validates successfully even though the profile is no longer an aggressive theme-overweight comparison档. The current tests catch the committed preset's sum-to-one and theme ordering, but they do not require `jsonschema.ValidationError` for these shadow-weight drift cases. This leaves the same schema-consumer trust gap that the previous Required was meant to close, only moved from `balanced` / `theme_off` to the two comparison profiles governed by §13.1 #28.

Materiality: `docs/us_short_system_design.md` makes `theme_plus` / `theme_aggressive` the shadow comparison tracks used to decide whether the main system is missing strong themes (§12.2), and §13.1 #28 explicitly routes comparison-profile weights and minimum comparison weeks through lifecycle calibration. Shadow tracks do not count toward ship-gate, but their future results can drive a reviewed promotion of the primary system. If a future comparison runner trusts schema validation and consumes non-normalized or non-theme-overweight weights, its evidence can be distorted while still appearing schema-valid.

Required repair: make the schema reject invalid `theme_plus` / `theme_aggressive` weight drift, not just the current preset tests. Preferred repair is to const-pin the current v1 prior weights (`theme_plus` 0.30/0.50/0.20; `theme_aggressive` 0.25/0.55/0.20) until a future reviewed §13 #28 calibration changes the schema/preset together, mirroring the local `egs_industry_heat_governance` precedent. If the implementer intentionally wants those two weights open, add an explicit structured rule (schema or a named validator consumed by future runners) that guarantees sum-to-one and preserves the intended ordering (`balanced.theme < theme_plus.theme < theme_aggressive.theme`, with nonnegative bounded weights) before any consumer can accept the artifact; document why exact const-pins are not used. Add negative tests requiring schema/validator rejection for at least `theme_plus` sum drift and `theme_aggressive` no-longer-aggressive drift. Boundary: schema / preset / scoring-profile tests / route-doc wording / this register only; do not implement batch 2 engine scoring, comparison-track runner, provider calls, DataHub, broker/order automation, market fetch, paper/live evidence, or ship-gate changes.

Finding (`R-USSHORT-SCORING-PROFILE-GOVERNANCE-SCHEMA-UNDERPINNED`): the current preset values match the design, but the schema is only a generic profile-shape schema and does not reject critical drift in the governed constants. Independent schema-only mutation probe accepted all of these invalid documents: `theme_plus.live_eligible=true`, `balanced.weights.theme=0.99`, `theme_off.weights={momentum:1.0, theme:0.0, catalyst:0.0}` (not the proportional rollback baseline), and `min_comparison_weeks=1`. The test file validates the current preset and catches some current-artifact drift by direct assertions, but it does not assert `jsonschema.ValidationError` for those schema-contract mutations, and a future consumer that trusts schema validation would accept them. Local precedent for this exact class is `schemas/egs_industry_heat_governance.schema.json`, which const-pins every governed profile weight and has a negative schema test for profile weight drift.

Materiality: `docs/us_short_system_design.md` makes `scoring_profile` a named governance contract: `balanced` is the only primary / only `model_paper` main track, `theme_plus` / `theme_aggressive` / `theme_off` are shadow-only, shadow never counts toward ship-gate, and `theme_off` is the attribution / rollback baseline with theme weight zero redistributed to momentum + catalyst. If schema validation accepts a shadow profile flipped live, a primary weight drift, a non-proportional `theme_off`, or a one-week comparison threshold, batch 2/3 code can later consume an invalid but schema-valid governance artifact and weaken the §4.2 / §12.2 / §18.1 #13/#24 isolation. A related routing gap is that the artifact exposes only `calibration_item_id=28`; design §13.1 #1 governs the primary 40/35/25 weight prior, while #28 governs comparison-profile weights and minimum comparison weeks. Collapsing both into #28 can make lifecycle reminders miss or duplicate the primary-weight calibration path.

Required repair: make the schema and tests reject the invalid governance states, not merely document them. Acceptable repair shapes: const-pin each named profile's role, live/shadow flags, and weights in the schema (or equivalent draft-07 `if/then`/per-profile definitions), require the initial comparison horizon to be at least / exactly 12 weeks per the frozen prior, and encode the calibration routing explicitly (for example `primary_weight_calibration_item_id=1` plus `comparison_profile_calibration_item_id=28`, or an equivalent unambiguous structure). Add negative tests that mutate the preset and require `jsonschema.ValidationError` for at least: shadow profile flipped live, balanced weight drift, `theme_off` non-proportional / non-zero-theme drift, and comparison weeks below 12; keep the current positive preset validation. Boundary: schema / preset / scoring-profile tests / route-doc wording / this register only; do not implement batch 2 engine scoring, comparison-track runner, provider calls, DataHub, broker/order automation, market fetch, paper/live evidence, or ship-gate changes.

Finding (`R-USSHORT-ACCTSTATE-TRADE-ACTION-VOCAB-DRIFT`): slice 1b claims `trades.csv.suggested_action` uses the §9 Chinese `final_action` vocabulary, but the implementation does not accept the design's exact non-fill value `否决/避开`. Evidence: `docs/us_short_system_design.md` §9 lists `final_action` as `建仓` / `加仓` / `减仓` / `清仓-止损` / `清仓-止盈` / `清仓-事件` / `持有` / `观察` / `否决/避开`; the changed route row also says `suggested_action` equals the §9 Chinese final_action vocab. In `runners/us_short_account_state_from_manual_tables.py`, `TRADE_NOFILL_ACTIONS = ("持有", "观察", "否决")`, so `TRADE_ACTIONS` omits `否决/避开`. Independent probe: `reconcile_trades_positions([{suggested_action="否决/避开", executed="FALSE", fill_price="", fill_shares="", skip_reason="avoid"}], ...)` raises `[FATAL] ... must be one of ... '否决'`, while the non-design alias `否决` is accepted. The current tests cover invalid English `buy` and executed `持有`, but do not cover the complete §9 action set or the `否决/避开` edge.

Materiality: `trades.csv` is the private manual actual / execution-log input for later reconciliation and live-normalized evidence. A user following the system design or a future weekly report that emits the documented §9 value `否决/避开` will fail conversion even though the row is contract-valid. Conversely, accepting `否决` without documenting it as an alias creates a second hidden vocabulary and weakens the no-dangling / schema-first boundary that batch 1 is meant to establish.

Required repair: make the action vocabulary single-sourced and tested before this slice can pass. Preferred repair is to accept the design-exact `否决/避开` as the canonical non-fill action; if `否决` is intentionally kept as a user-input alias, document that alias explicitly and test both the canonical value and alias behavior without changing the stored action silently. Add adversarial tests covering every §9 action value, especially `否决/避开` as `executed=FALSE` with `skip_reason`, and preserve the existing executed/non-executed fill invariants. Update `trades.csv` template / README wording only if the canonical vocabulary is deliberately changed in the design. Boundary: converter, tests, CSV example, route docs, and this register only; do not implement batch 3 ship-gate evidence consumption, provider calls, DataHub, broker/order automation, market fetch, A-share crossing, short-selling support, or live trading.

Chose the preferred repair (design-exact canonical value, NO `否决` alias): `TRADE_NOFILL_ACTIONS = ("持有", "观察", "否决/避开")`. RESOLVED P1 (2026-06-20): US-short batch 1 slice 1a manual CSV accepts unknown columns and silently drops them. status `resolved`(working tree; 用户 `修复` 即授权; pending Codex re-`审查 PASS` + 用户 `提交`); Required ID `R-USSHORT-ACCTSTATE-UNKNOWN-CSV-COLUMNS-SILENT-DROP`; severity `P1` (manual account-state contract integrity / future weekly sizing input; can misstate holding direction before any consumer gets a chance to validate it). Scope reviewed: full first-slice re-review of the current dirty US-short account-state implementation, including `runners/us_short_account_state_from_manual_tables.py`, account-state and lineage schemas/examples/templates, tests, `docs/README.md`, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`, `.gitignore` private-path behavior, and this register. The previous four account-state Required repairs are verified closed in the working tree: no in-repo nonprivate override, validator rejects impossible/future dates, register boundary is current, and cash must be `<= bucket`.

Finding (`R-USSHORT-ACCTSTATE-UNKNOWN-CSV-COLUMNS-SILENT-DROP`): the converter only checks that required CSV columns exist; it does not reject unknown columns in either the CSV reader path or the pure `build_account_state` table path. Evidence: `_read_csv_table` builds `header`, checks `missing`, then returns stripped row dicts without checking extras (`runners/us_short_account_state_from_manual_tables.py` lines 317-324). `_build_account_fields` and `_build_positions` then consume only known keys and ignore the rest (lines 198-231). Independent probe: a `positions.csv` row with extra `direction=short` and an `account.csv` row with extra `unexpected_account_flag` are accepted by `main`, and the output position becomes `{"direction": "long", ...}`; the pure `build_account_state` path accepts the same extra keys as well.

Materiality: slice 1a is the manual account-state contract that future US-short weekly holding re-evaluation and sizing will consume. The design says positions.csv has the fixed fields `ticker / shares / avg_cost_usd / entry_date / current_stop / notes`, v1 is long-only with `direction=long` as a marked door, and malformed/out-of-contract input must fail fast rather than silently degrade. If a user tries to record a short/borrowed position by adding `direction=short`, or adds an unsupported account/sizing field, the converter silently drops that fact and emits a long position. That can make the future report treat a short exposure as a long holding; tests currently cover schema additionalProperties only after JSON is produced, not unknown CSV headers before production.

Required repair: make the input contract strict before this slice can pass. Reject any unknown CSV header for `account.csv` and `positions.csv` (including row overflow represented by `None` keys from `csv.DictReader`), and reject unknown keys in the pure `build_account_state` table path too so tests/future callers cannot bypass the CSV gate. Keep the allowed optional columns (`portfolio_total_equity` for account; `current_stop` and `notes` for positions) and all current valid templates green. Add adversarial tests for at least: positions extra `direction=short` rejected; account extra unknown field rejected; CSV row with too many cells rejected; pure table path extra key rejected. Boundary: account-state converter/schema-doc wording/tests/register only; do not implement slice 1b trades reconciliation, short-channel support, provider calls, DataHub, broker/order automation, market fetch, paper/live evidence, or ship-gate changes.

Resolution (Claude `修复` 2026-06-20, working tree; 用户 `修复` 即授权; status `resolved` until Codex re-`审查 PASS` + 用户 `提交`): judged valid and accepted — I had applied the design's fail-fast principle to VALUES (anti-Excel-coercion) but not to STRUCTURE (columns/keys), so an out-of-contract column (e.g. `direction=short`, which v1 long-only would silently emit as long) was dropped. Added `EXPECTED_COLUMNS` (allowed = required + optional: account = the six §3.6 fields incl. optional `portfolio_total_equity`; positions = ticker/shares/avg_cost_usd/entry_date + optional current_stop/notes) and `_reject_unknown_columns` (rejects any column not in the allowed set, and treats the `csv.DictReader` `None` restkey — row-overflow cells — as unknown). Enforced on BOTH paths: `_read_csv_table` rejects an unknown CSV header (catches header-level extras even for a 0-row CSV) and `build_account_state` rejects unknown row keys (covers the pure-dict caller path + the `None` restkey from a too-many-cells row, so neither the CSV gate nor the pure path is a bypass). Tests: `test_positions_extra_direction_column_rejected` (the named short case), `test_account_extra_unknown_column_rejected`, `test_pure_path_extra_key_rejected`, `test_main_rejects_unknown_csv_column` (CSV header), `test_main_rejects_row_with_too_many_cells` (None restkey). Class-complete (pre-Codex checklist A — cover the malformed-structure / silent-drop CLASS, not just the named instance): also reject a duplicate CSV header (`csv.DictReader` keeps only the last same-named column, silently dropping the other column's data) — `_read_csv_table` raises on dupes, `test_main_rejects_duplicate_header`. The committed templates / happy path stay green (their columns are exactly the allowed set). Verify: account-state converter+schema+doc/route guards 93 OK; full discover `python -m unittest discover -s tests` 2832 OK (zero regression; +6 net) in a runtime with deps (a dep-light runtime RED is environmental, unrelated A-short imports); `py_compile` OK; `git diff --check` clean except CRLF; BOM/FFFD=0; no provider/broker/market-fetch/slice-1b/short-channel introduced. Closure on Codex re-`审查 PASS` + 用户 `提交`.

RESOLVED P1 (2026-06-20): US-short batch 1 slice 1a account-state cash/bucket ceiling gap. status `resolved`(working tree; 用户 `修复` 即授权; pending Codex re-`审查 PASS` + 用户 `提交`); Required ID `R-USSHORT-ACCTSTATE-CASH-BUCKET-CEILING-GAP`; severity `P1` (capital-policy / cross-bucket cash isolation before the weekly sizing consumer exists). Scope reviewed: current dirty tree for US-short account-state slice (`runners/us_short_account_state_from_manual_tables.py`, `schemas/us_short_account_state.schema.json`, lineage schema/examples/templates/tests, `docs/README.md`, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`, and this register). The previous three account-state Required repairs are verified closed in the working tree: no in-repo nonprivate override surface remains, validator rejects impossible/future dates, and the register boundary now distinguishes original docs-only landing from current slice 1a code.

Finding (`R-USSHORT-ACCTSTATE-CASH-BUCKET-CEILING-GAP`): `build_account_state` and `validate_account_state` accept `us_short_available_cash` greater than the computed `us_short_bucket_capital`. Independent probe: `us_market_equity=30000` produces `us_short_bucket_capital=10000`, but `us_short_available_cash=50000` builds and validates successfully (`cash_gt_bucket=ACCEPTED {"cash": 50000.0, "bucket": 10000.0}`). The schema only enforces cash `>= 0`; the validator only enforces `bucket == us_market_equity/3`, unique tickers, long-only, and date/PIT validity.

Materiality: this account-state schema is the future weekly sizing input, and the project-level capital policy says each market is split into 1/3 long / 1/3 short / 1/3 liquidity, A/US cash is non-fungible, and each runner must have a capital ceiling not exceeding its bucket. The US-short design also says the short bucket is computed from `us_market_equity/3`, and global cash allocation later consumes available cash. Accepting an account state where bucket-local cash exceeds the bucket can silently mix US-long / liquidity cash into US-short sizing unless every future consumer re-caps the field defensively. The safer contract is to reject the inconsistent state at the manual-input boundary.

Resolution (Claude `修复` 2026-06-20, working tree; 用户 `修复` 即授权; status `resolved` until Codex re-`审查 PASS` + 用户 `提交`): judged valid and accepted — bucket-local cash exceeding the bucket would let US-long / liquidity cash silently mix into US-short sizing (capital policy: per-market 1/3 buckets, A/US cash non-fungible, runner ceiling <= its bucket). Enforced `us_short_available_cash <= us_short_bucket_capital` at BOTH boundaries: `build_account_state` rejects it at CSV build (after computing bucket) and `validate_account_state` rejects it too (so a hand-edited / non-builder JSON is caught by the single-source gate); both use the `_REL_EPS * max(1, bucket)` tolerance so `cash == bucket` (a fully-cash bucket) is allowed and only a meaningful excess is rejected. The schema description of `us_short_available_cash` now documents the cross-field invariant. Tests: `test_cash_exceeds_bucket_fatal` (build), `test_cash_equals_bucket_ok` (boundary positive control), `test_cash_exceeds_bucket_rejected_by_validator` (validator). Scope of the invariant (deliberate): only `cash <= bucket` is enforced (cash is part of the bucket). A `sum(positions avg_cost_usd * shares) + cash <= bucket` check is NOT added, because `avg_cost_usd` is a cost basis, not current market value, and the bucket is a forward capital allocation — that stricter check would falsely reject legitimately appreciated holdings; the runner-level sizing ceiling against current value belongs to the future weekly sizing consumer, not the manual-input contract. B-ripple caught + fixed: the pre-existing `test_bucket_is_equity_over_three` used equity=1000 (bucket≈333) with the default cash 4000, which the new invariant correctly rejected, so that test's cash was lowered to 100. Verify: account-state converter+schema+doc/route guards 87 OK; full discover `python -m unittest discover -s tests` 2826 OK in a runtime with jsonschema/requests/tushare (zero regression; +3 net) — full discover can be RED in a dependency-light runtime due to unrelated A-short requests/tushare imports + `pro=None`, which is environmental, not this slice; `py_compile` OK; `git diff --check` clean except CRLF; BOM/FFFD=0; no provider/broker/market-fetch introduced. Closure on Codex re-`审查 PASS` + 用户 `提交`.

Required repair: enforce the account-state capital invariant before this slice can pass: `us_short_available_cash <= us_short_bucket_capital` (within a small numeric tolerance) in both the CSV builder path and `validate_account_state`, so hand-edited JSON is also rejected. If the implementer believes a different model is needed, split the meaning explicitly (for example, raw account cash vs bucket-local deployable cash) and ensure the field consumed by future US-short sizing is capped to the bucket; do not keep the current ambiguous accepted state. Add builder-level and validator-level tests proving cash above bucket is rejected, keep zero cash valid, and update schema/docs wording if needed so the contract is clear. Boundary: account-state schema/converter/tests/docs/register only; do not implement slice 1b trades reconciliation, provider calls, DataHub consumption, broker/order automation, market fetch, paper/live evidence, or ship-gate changes.

Finding 1 (`R-USSHORT-ACCTSTATE-PRIVATE-OUTPUT-OVERRIDE-BYPASS`, severity P0 security / private-account hygiene): the new converter's fail-closed path guard can be bypassed for an in-repo non-gitignored output by passing `--allow-nonprivate-account-out`. Evidence: `_reject_nonprivate_account_output_path` returns before `git check-ignore` enforcement when `allow_nonprivate=True`, the CLI exposes that flag, and `tests/test_us_short_account_state_from_manual_tables.py::PrivacyGuardTests::test_allow_override_ok` locks the bypass in as a passing behavior. This conflicts with `docs/us_short_system_design.md` §11.6 / §18.1 #1, which says private outputs inside the repo and not ignored must fail-fast by `git check-ignore` truth, and it can write holdings / cash / cost into a tracked path such as `docs/*.json`.

Required repair 1: remove the in-repo nonprivate override, or restrict any deliberate export escape hatch to paths outside the repo only. In-repo non-gitignored paths must fail regardless of CLI flags. OPEN P1 (2026-06-19): A-long value-yield forward-paper data-layer industry-membership + active/delisted classification + index_member_all provider-contract gap. Required ID `R-ALONG-VY-FP-DATALAYER-INDUSTRY-CLASSIFICATION-CONTRACT-GAP`; status `resolved` (committed master 2026-06-20: code @e5bd1902, review docs @7b1280bf; Codex round-3 PASS); severity `P1`; scope reviewed: `runners/a_long_large_cap_value_yield_forward_paper_data_layer.py`, `runners/a_long_large_cap_value_yield_forward_paper_capture.py`, `tests/test_a_long_value_yield_forward_paper_data_layer.py`, `tests/test_a_long_value_yield_forward_paper_capture.py`; consumed frozen owners `runners/a_long_full_main_board_signal_search.py` (`industry_context_for_symbol`/`build_signal_context`/`load_industry_records`), `runners/a_long_full_main_board_materialization_packet.py` (bulk `index_member_all`); PIT label `A-long value-yield forward PAPER / lean data layer / SW industry membership / active-delisted classification / index_member_all provider shape / first-capture robustness`. Reviewer: Claude acting-as-reviewer (user-authorized, because Codex mistakenly performed the `修复` as implementer).

Finding 1 (P1 / execution correctness + false contract): an active top-500 symbol with no SW industry-membership row makes `assemble_forward_inputs` ABORT, not gracefully exclude. Evidence: `forward_scored_items` (`data_layer.py` ~146) calls `base.industry_context_for_symbol`; the frozen function (`a_long_full_main_board_signal_search.py` ~822-825) RAISES `ValueError: active investable symbol has no industry membership source` when `industry_source=="missing"` (zero membership rows) and the symbol is active — it only returns `industry_excluded=True` for `no_interval_membership` or `exception_symbols`. Independent probe reproduced the abort for one active name with empty `index_member_records`. The data-layer docstring (~98-100) claims "缺成员的票 industry_context 标 excluded → 零误纳", which is FALSE. Materiality: the layer bypasses `base.load_industry_records`'s SW-repair supplement; the frozen full-main-board run needed per-symbol SW supplementation for 1189/3200 active names (`docs/a_long_main_board_sw_coverage_repair_execution_summary_20260604.json`), so bulk membership does not cover most names → the first real capture (`as_of>=20260630`) is at material risk of aborting on the first top-500 name lacking a membership row. Required repair: handle missing membership per the frozen contract — route missing-membership symbols into `exception_symbols` (so the frozen fn returns `industry_excluded=True`), or explicitly skip/exclude items with `industry_source=="missing"` in the data layer; fix the false docstring; do NOT rely on the frozen fn to "mark excluded" for `missing`. Also carry the frozen `industry_excluded` 4th return value onto each scored item (currently discarded at `data_layer.py` ~146) so `add_industry_neutral_scores` parity holds if `exception_symbols` ever non-empty (today hardcoded `frozenset()`).

Finding 2 (P1 / data contract / classification axis): `build_forward_context` (`data_layer.py` ~114-116) sets `active_symbols`/`delisted_symbols` from `delist_date is None` / `is not None`, but the frozen `base.build_signal_context` (~499-541) derives them from `stock_basic` list_status (`L` vs `D`). A still-trading `L`-status name with a FUTURE `delist_date` is `active` in the frozen contract but lands in `delisted_symbols` here. Probe: `delist_date=20251231`, `as_of=20240628` → `active=[]`, `delisted=[600000.SH]` (wrong). `active_symbols` feeds the Finding-1 missing-membership branch, so the mis-axis interacts with the abort path. Latent today (most L rows have empty delist_date) but a real divergence. Required repair: classify active/delisted by security-master origin (L vs D set), not by `delist_date is None`; `fetch_forward_panel` already separates `basic_l`/`basic_d` then merges and loses the distinction — thread the origin through.

Finding 3 (P2 material-for-first-run / provider contract): `fetch_forward_panel` calls `pro.index_member_all(ts_code=symbol, ...)` per symbol and a lineage guard asserts each row's `ts_code == symbol`, but the frozen materialization pulls SW membership via one BULK `index_member_all` (fields only, no ts_code filter) and the constituent stock may live in a separate field (Tushare `index_member_all` ts_code conventionally filters by INDEX code, constituent in `con_code`). If so, the per-symbol filter + lineage assertion + `industry_records_by_symbol` grouping (all assuming `ts_code==stock`) raise or mis-group at first real call. The "现写现验" provider-shape risk, but the most fragile call in the plan. Required repair: verify the real `index_member_all` route/params/field at first capture; prefer the bulk pull keyed on the constituent field; relax the per-symbol lineage guard accordingly.

Optional (non-blocking, P2): (O1) `validate_accumulator_consistency` only constrains the PRIMARY construction's `matured_cohort_count` vs actual-504-matured; a forged DIAGNOSTIC `matured_cohort_count=99` (real 0) is accepted (probe confirmed). Diagnostics never feed the promote gate, but the validator claims to fail-closed against drift artifacts; extend the `actual_matured` check to all three constructions (~3 lines). (O2) `main()` constructs the tushare client before `_validate_capture_args` (init makes no network call, cosmetic); call the arg guard before client init. (O3) `FORWARD_REQUIRED_FIELDS["index_member_all"]` requires `l1_code`/`l2_code` but frozen `industry_for_symbol` accepts `l1_name`/`l2_name` alone — stricter than needed (internally consistent, won't fire); the `约 4N+2P` comment under-counts the +5 bulk constant (code reconciliation correct). (O4) `forward_rolling_relative_nav_drawdown` uses month-end checkpoints while entry is the next open day → single-cohort intra-window drawdown reads understated/None and the `-0.15` floor uses a coarse lower-bound (bias toward promote, the unsafe direction). PARITY-FAITHFUL (frozen `bf.rolling_relative_nav_drawdown` uses identical `sorted(MONTHLY_AS_OF_DATES)` checkpoints), NOT introduced here, and promote is advisory-only; document `rolling_relative_nav_max_drawdown` as a monthly-checkpoint lower-bound or add finer checkpoints if a tighter gate is wanted. (O5) test blind spots: no end-to-end promote through real `build_forward_accumulator`, no real-data mixed-exit propagation, no missing-membership / future-delist test (the classes of Findings 1-2) — add them.

Finding 1 (P1 / data integrity / PIT frozen snapshot): `build_cohort_snapshot()` records `entry_date` for each frozen cohort construction, but `backfill_cohort()` recomputes the entry date from the current `trade_dates` on every backfill. Evidence: `runners/a_long_large_cap_value_yield_forward_paper_capture.py::build_cohort_snapshot` sets `entry_date = _first_trade_day_after(as_of, trade_dates)` and stores it; `backfill_cohort()` later sets a fresh `entry_date = _first_trade_day_after(as_of, trade_dates)` and uses that derived index. Materiality: a forward-paper cohort's entry anchor is part of the frozen monthly snapshot. If a later calendar source or price-cache date set changes, historical cohorts can be re-anchored silently, contaminating OOS evidence while still passing tests and accumulator validation. Required repair: `backfill_cohort()` must use the saved cohort construction `entry_date` as the anchor, validate that it is present when `entry_status == "ok"`, validate it is in `trade_dates`, and fail-closed or explicitly mark unbackfillable if a recomputed first-open date disagrees with the frozen entry. Add adversarial tests for a shifted `trade_dates` list / stored-entry mismatch and a positive test for stable frozen-entry backfill.

Finding 2 (P1 / return lineage / delist and missing-exit semantics): `base.compute_return()` returns the actual benchmark exit date after `resolve_return_dates()` handles scheduled exit, `terminal_last_trade_before_delist`, and `next_available_after_missing_scheduled_exit`, but the new `backfill_cohort()` discards those returned dates and always records the scheduled `trade_dates[exit_idx]` with `exit_policy = "scheduled_exit_basket_equal_weight"`. Evidence: `runners/a_long_full_main_board_signal_search.py::resolve_return_dates` has non-scheduled exit policies; `compute_return()` returns `(stock_return, benchmark_return, entry_date, benchmark_exit_date)`; `runners/a_long_large_cap_value_yield_forward_paper_capture.py::backfill_cohort` assigns `_e, _x` then writes scheduled exit metadata. Materiality: delist, halt, missing scheduled close, or terminal last-trade outcomes are central A-long data-integrity and survivorship risks. Recording them as ordinary scheduled exits makes the accumulator look cleaner than the actual evidence path. Required repair: preserve actual exit metadata from the frozen return resolver. At minimum, record the actual exit date used for the basket; if basket members use mixed exit policies/dates, encode a fail-closed or explicit mixed/member-audit policy rather than labeling the whole basket as scheduled. Add tests covering terminal delist / missing scheduled exit and the legal scheduled case.

Finding 3 (P1 / provider/data contract / execution gate): `fetch_forward_panel()` directly calls live Tushare endpoints without the call-plan protections used by prior A-long materialization slices: no explicit `start_date`/`end_date` on per-symbol fundamentals/prices/benchmark, no minimum-field validation before assembly, no pacing/budget envelope, no raw-payload or no-raw tracked-summary boundary, and no kwargs assertions in tests. Evidence: the new data layer calls `pro.cashflow(ts_code=...)`, `pro.income(ts_code=...)`, `pro.daily(ts_code=...)`, `pro.adj_factor(ts_code=...)`, `pro.index_daily(ts_code=...)`, `pro.index_member_all()`, `pro.namechange(...)`, and `pro.trade_cal(...)` with mostly fields-only args; the older A-long materialization packet records date windows, minimum fields, and `NetworkPacer` boundaries. Materiality: the prereg requires monthly PIT pulls, frozen top-500 universe, real delist/halt/merger outcomes, and separate user authorization before each fetch. A loose live-fetch wrapper can pull provider defaults, incomplete windows, or malformed fields and still assemble a seemingly valid paper accumulator. Required repair: add a narrow forward-capture call-plan contract for this lean slice: explicit date windows sufficient for TTM and all open horizons/backfill price history, minimum fields per endpoint, call count/budget, pacing or documented no-pacing decision, raw/gitignored or no-raw tracked summary policy, and tests asserting the fake provider receives those kwargs and that missing required fields fail before accumulator write.

Materiality: this is lower than the backfill/data-contract issues because the runner still requires both confirmation flags and remains research-only, but it can create a paper artifact for a non-month-end date or outside the intended research path. Required repair: add fail-closed guards for `as_of >= 20260630`, month-end-open decision semantics where feasible from the fetched calendar / trade dates, and a research-only output path rule or explicit refusal of production `result/` paths. OPEN P1 (2026-06-19): A-long large-cap value-yield forward-paper accumulator schema promotion gate gap. Required ID `R-ALONG-VY-FP-ACCUMULATOR-SCHEMA-PROMOTION-GATE-GAP`; status `resolved` (Codex re-`审查 PASS` + committed master dcb33dd 2026-06-19); severity `P1`; scope reviewed: `schemas/a_long_large_cap_value_yield_forward_paper_accumulator.schema.json`, `schemas/a_long_large_cap_value_yield_forward_paper_tracking.schema.json`, `research/preregistrations/a_long_large_cap_value_yield_forward_paper_tracking_20260609.json`, `research/ledgers/a_long_large_cap_value_yield_forward_paper_tracking_program_test_budget_ledger_20260609.json`, `tests/schema/test_a_long_large_cap_value_yield_forward_paper_tracking_schema.py`, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`; PIT label `A-long value-yield forward PAPER / accumulator schema / promotion-read gate / no best-of-three / monthly capture artifact`.

Finding: the new untracked accumulator schema is syntactically valid JSON and passes `Draft7Validator.check_schema()`, but it does not enforce the frozen forward-paper decision contract strongly enough. Independent jsonschema probes showed the schema accepts an accumulator with `paper_read.matured_cohort_count=0`, `read_available=false`, and `routing="promote_eligible_pending_new_reviewed_real_money_prereg"`. The same accepted artifact also marks `cash_flow_to_circ_mv` as `primary_promotion_construction` in `construction_metrics`, even though the reviewed prereg freezes only `value_yield_composite_cf_sales` as promotion-eligible. A second accepted artifact includes a cohort before the `20260630` start floor, `interim_horizons_trading_days=[999]`, horizon key `"999"`, `basket_size=20` with `selected_symbols=[]`, and a `matured` horizon with `relative_excess_net=null` / no exit date.

Materiality: this is not a data-fetch or runner execution bug yet; the file is currently untracked and no capture runner is present. It is still material because this schema is the future official accumulator contract for a forward-paper promotion-read artifact. If committed as-is, a future runner or hand-built artifact could claim promotion eligibility with insufficient cohorts, wrong primary construction, malformed baskets, or non-matured return evidence while still passing schema validation. That weakens the reviewed anti-best-of-three / single-primary / paper-only governance from the 20260609 prereg and could misroute a later real-money forward-live prereg decision.

Required repair: tighten the accumulator schema and add adversarial schema tests. At minimum: enforce exactly the three construction IDs where applicable; bind `promotion_role` to `construction_id` so only `value_yield_composite_cf_sales` can be `primary_promotion_construction` and the two single yields are diagnostic only; constrain interim horizon list and horizon property names to the frozen set (`21`, `63`, `126`, `252`, `504` as applicable); reject `routing=promote_eligible...` unless `read_available=true`, primary matured cohorts meet the 12-cohort minimum, and persistence/drawdown booleans are true; reject `insufficient_cohorts` when the read says enough cohorts; require matured horizon records to have numeric `relative_excess_net` and concrete exit metadata; prevent pre-start-floor cohorts; require selected symbol uniqueness and consistency with `basket_size` or a documented status-specific zero-basket shape; pin required source refs for prereg, ledger, batch execution summary, and schema/design refs. Add planted-failure tests for each of the accepted bad probes above plus positive tests for legal pending and legal matured artifacts.

Boundary: do not fetch data, run capture, spend the singleton ledger, change the frozen prereg construction, change thresholds/horizons/benchmarks/universe, promote a single-factor view, claim alpha validation, production readiness, ship-gate evidence, real-money readiness, full-size use, DataHub readiness, or broker/order automation in this repair. This is a schema/test repair only unless separately approved.

Required ID `R-ASHORT-S3B-R4B-RATCHET-INVARIANT-GUARD-GAP`; status `resolved` (Codex re-`审查 PASS` + committed master 9e5c10c 2026-06-19); severity `P2`; scope reviewed: `runners/a_short_phase5_engine.py`, `runners/a_short_weekly_pipeline.py`, `schemas/a_short_m67_report.schema.json`, `schemas/a_short_holding_ratchet.schema.json`, `tests/test_a_short_gap_data_registry.py`, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`; PIT label `A-short S3b R4b / machine.ratchet / ratcheted_stop null / effective-stop invariant / save envelope`.

Finding: the previous duplicate-key sidecar read gap is addressed in the current working tree: `load_holding_ratchet()` now rejects duplicate `(ts_code, entry_date)` before dict folding and rejects row `last_as_of > envelope as_of`. The remaining material gap is the in-report ratchet invariant. `_ratchet_report_error()` says `ratcheted_stop` must be at least the current-week effective stop (`max(S3a plan.stop, R4a breakeven)`), but its check is `if eff and _is_finite_num(rs) and rs < max(eff)`, so `ratcheted_stop=None` skips the comparison. Independent probe built a held M6.7 report with `machine.entry_exit_size_star.plan.stop=3.05` and `machine.ratchet.ratcheted_stop=None`; both `validate_m67_consistency()` and official `write_m67_report()` accepted it (`write_m67_ratchet_null_stop=ACCEPTED plan_stop=3.05`). Materiality: normal `_apply_holding_ratchet()` currently computes a finite `ratcheted_stop` when the current report has a finite S3a stop or R4a breakeven, so this is not a normal happy-path output bug. It is still material because R4b is a cross-week holding-state contract and `write_m67_report()` is the official write boundary. A hand-built report or future builder drift can hide the protective ratchet stop as `null` even though the current-week stop exists, weakening the "ratchet contains current week effective stop / only-up stop" invariant that downstream review and the user-facing report rely on. The save-time envelope gap is a fail-closed/documentation mismatch: it will be caught on the next load, but it should not be written by the sidecar writer in the first place.

Required repair: strengthen `_ratchet_report_error()` so when current-week effective stop exists, `ratcheted_stop` must be a finite number and `>= max(effective_stop)`; `None` / non-finite must raise. Keep `ratcheted_stop=None` legal only when there is no finite S3a stop, no finite R4a breakeven, and no finite prior ratcheted stop. Add adversarial tests proving `validate_m67_consistency()` and `write_m67_report()` reject `ratcheted_stop=None` when `plan.stop` exists, while the legal no-effective-stop null case still passes if expected by design. Add a save-time PIT envelope guard in `save_holding_ratchet()` for row `last_as_of <= as_of` (or narrow the schema/docstring claim if the design intentionally relies on load-only rejection), with a direct writer test.

OPEN P2 (2026-06-19): A-short S3b R4b ratchet sidecar duplicate-key PIT bypass. Required ID `R-ASHORT-S3B-R4B-RATCHET-SIDECAR-DUPLICATE-PIT-BYPASS`; status `resolved` (Codex re-`审查 PASS` + committed master 9e5c10c 2026-06-19); severity `P2`; scope reviewed: `.gitignore`, `runners/a_short_phase5_engine.py`, `runners/a_short_weekly_pipeline.py`, `runners/a_short_m67_render.py`, `schemas/a_short_m67_report.schema.json`, `schemas/a_short_holding_ratchet.schema.json`, `schemas/examples/a_short_gap_data_field_registry.example.json`, `tests/test_a_short_gap_data_registry.py`, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`; PIT label `A-short S3b R4b / holding ratchet sidecar / duplicate key / future-state guard bypass`.

Finding: R4b correctly adds a gitignored private sidecar route and normal builder tests pass for bootstrap, re-entry, same-week idempotence, future `last_as_of` rejection, only-up stop, only-up disposition, and render. The material gap is in sidecar read validation. `schemas/a_short_holding_ratchet.schema.json` says `(ts_code, entry_date)` rows are unique, and `load_holding_ratchet()` says it validates the sidecar to prevent damaged / hand-edited state. But `load_holding_ratchet()` returns a dict comprehension keyed by `ts_code|entry_date`, so duplicate rows silently overwrite earlier rows before `_apply_holding_ratchet()` checks `last_as_of > as_of`. Independent probe created a schema-valid sidecar with two rows for `600000.SH|20260601`: first row `last_as_of=20991231`, second row `last_as_of=20260610`. `load_holding_ratchet()` kept only the second row, and `_apply_holding_ratchet(..., as_of=20260617)` accepted the state instead of rejecting the hidden future row.

Materiality: normal `save_holding_ratchet()` currently writes from a dict, so ordinary system output is unique. This is still material because R4b is a cross-week PIT state file. A damaged, manually edited, merge-conflicted, or future-writer sidecar can hide future state behind a later duplicate row and bypass the very guard intended to prevent future-contaminated ratchet decisions. Since the sidecar contains real holding state and feeds future weekly reports, read-time corruption must fail closed.

Required repair: make the sidecar reader/writer fail closed on duplicate identity and PIT envelope corruption. At minimum, `load_holding_ratchet()` must iterate rows, compute `_holding_ratchet_key(ts_code, entry_date)`, and raise on any duplicate key before returning the dict. Add an adversarial test where a duplicate key hides a future `last_as_of` row and assert load/apply rejects it. Prefer also checking row `last_as_of <= top-level as_of` at load time and adding a schema/runtime note that composite uniqueness is enforced in Python, not JSON schema draft-07.

Boundary: do not change R4b only-up math, re-entry semantics, same-week idempotence, R4a price-cross / breakeven logic, S3a price formulas, `table.损` / `plan.stop`, `操作` enum, EGS / TopN / selection / share-size / hard-veto behavior, broker/order behavior, provider calls, or sidecar privacy route without separate approval. OPEN P2 (2026-06-19): A-short S3b R3 explicit-null price no-dangling guard gap. Required ID `R-ASHORT-S3B-R3-EXPLICIT-NULL-PRICE-GUARD-GAP`; status `resolved` (Codex re-`审查 PASS` + committed master 8869e8d 2026-06-19); severity `P2`; scope reviewed: `runners/a_short_phase5_engine.py`, `runners/a_short_m67_render.py`, `runners/a_short_weekly_pipeline.py`, `schemas/a_short_m67_report.schema.json`, `schemas/examples/a_short_gap_data_field_registry.example.json`, `tests/test_a_short_gap_data_registry.py`, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`; untracked excluded byproduct `research/results/a_short/iv_feed_20260605/iv_feed.json`; PIT label `A-short S3b R3 / held advisory prices / explicit-null no-dangling / validator field-presence guard`.

Finding: S3b R3 correctly extends normal builder output for held rows: `clear_review` writes `table.清仓价 == S3a plan.stop`, `reduce_review` writes `table.减仓价 == S3a plan.t1` plus `table.减仓比例 == "1/3"`, and schema/render can display those advisory fields. The material gap is in write-time validation when the referenced S3a price is unavailable (`plan.t1 is None` for breached reduce, or `plan is None` for no-price clear). `validate_m67_consistency()` compares with `tbl.get(...)` / `mc.get(...)`, so it treats an omitted field and an explicit `null` as equivalent. Independent probes accepted: (1) a breached `reduce_review` held report after deleting `table.减仓价` and `machine.reduce_price` while keeping `减仓比例="1/3"`; (2) a no-price `clear_review` held report after deleting `table.清仓价` and `machine.clear_price`; (3) a non-held candidate report carrying `machine.reduce_price = null`.

Materiality: normal `_apply_holding_disposition()` currently emits explicit `null`, so this is not a normal builder-output failure. It is still material because R3's contract is explicitly no-dangling: when S3a cannot compute the advisory price, the user-visible output must say the price was not computed, not silently omit the field. The renderer only shows "未算出" when the table key exists. A future builder drift or hand-built report can therefore pass validation while hiding the missing reduce/clear price, and non-held rows can carry R3 machine fields despite the held-only claim.

Required repair: strengthen `validate_m67_consistency()` (or an equivalent write-time guard) to distinguish field absence from explicit `null`. For `clear_review`, require the `清仓价` table key and `machine.clear_price` key to be present, with value exactly `S3a plan.stop` (including explicit `None` when plan is absent/unavailable), and reject `减仓价` / `减仓比例` / reduce machine fields. For `reduce_review`, require the `减仓价`, `减仓比例`, `machine.reduce_price`, and `machine.reduce_ratio` keys to be present, with `减仓价 == S3a plan.t1` (including explicit `None`) and ratio equal to the advisory fixed档; reject `清仓价` / clear machine fields. For other held signals, reject any R3 table or machine field even when the value is `None`. For non-held rows, reject any R3 table or machine field by key presence, not only non-null values. Add adversarial tests for missing explicit null reduce price, missing explicit null clear price when plan is absent, missing machine null while table null exists, stray clear/reduce machine null on the wrong disposition, and non-held `machine.reduce_price = None`.

Boundary: do not change S3a price formulas, stop/t1/t2 semantics, `操作` enum, EGS / TopN / selection / share-size / hard-veto behavior, reducer/clear automatic actions, broker/order behavior, provider calls, R4 active-action / ratchet behavior, or the fixed advisory ratio without separate approval. Keep `research/results/a_short/iv_feed_20260605/iv_feed.json` excluded from commit.

Resolution (Claude `修复`, working tree 2026-06-19; status `open` until Codex re-`审查 PASS` + user `提交`): made R3 price validation distinguish field absence from explicit null via key presence (`validate_m67_consistency`, `runners/a_short_phase5_engine.py`). (1) Held branch now asserts the EXACT R3 key-set per disposition: `clear_review` ⟹ table has exactly {`清仓价`} + machine {`clear_price`}; `reduce_review` ⟹ table {`减仓价`,`减仓比例`} + machine {`reduce_price`,`reduce_ratio`}; other held signals ⟹ empty. A missing `清仓价`/`减仓价` key (even when the referenced S3a price is `None`) is now rejected, and stray wrong-disposition keys (including present-but-`None`) are rejected. Value checks unchanged (`清仓价==plan.stop`, `减仓价==plan.t1` incl. explicit `None`, ratio==advisory档) + machine↔table equality. Required repair: distinguish "provider returned an empty list" from "provider returned rows but zero PIT-valid rows." For `income` / `balancesheet`, a non-empty provider result that leaves no PIT-valid realized periods must become per-key `unchecked_codes` or the whole section `unknown_or_unavailable`, not `checked` empty. Required ID `R-ASHORT-GAP42-ROUND5-FINANCIAL-QUALITY-CANDIDATE-SCOPE-GUARD-GAP`; status `resolved` (Codex re-`审查 PASS` + committed master 8fadd7a 2026-06-18); severity `P2`; scope reviewed: `runners/a_short_weekly_pipeline.py`, `runners/a_short_phase5_engine.py`, `schemas/examples/a_short_gap_data_field_registry.example.json`, `tests/test_a_short_gap_data_registry.py`, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`; design source reviewed: `C:\Users\cnhea\Desktop\4.2.md` decision 5 / financial-quality sequencing / comparison-only boundary; excluded untracked byproduct `research/results/a_short/iv_feed_20260605/iv_feed.json`; PIT label `A-short 4.2 / financial_quality first cut / candidate-only scope / no-dangling guard`.

Finding: the implementation direction is acceptable in purpose. `normalize_candidate()` passes existing `fundamental.profitability` / `fundamental.quality` / `scores.l2_flags` into `financial_quality`; `_financial_quality_operation_impacts()` emits a non-production advisory `operation_impact` only for red flags; `build_m67_report()` lands it in `精简结论区.风控触发`; and the current builder does not emit this impact for held positions. The material gap is the write-time guard. `validate_operation_impact_no_dangling()` says financial_quality is "候选 only", but it only checks `field_class`, `production_effect_enabled`, `veto_class`, `new_entry_effect`, `holding_effect`, and the visible marker. It does not require `visibility_shape="candidate_row_impact"`, `impact_scope="new_entry"`, `privacy_class="public_tracked"`, or `position_state != "held"`. Independent mutation probe accepted a held report carrying `source_field="financial_quality"` with `visibility_shape="holding_row_impact"`, `impact_scope="existing_holding"`, `privacy_class="private_account"`, and the risk marker.

Materiality: this slice explicitly declares the first cut is candidate-only and that holding financial-quality handling is left to a later slice. 4.2 also keeps S3b / holding active management behind a separate approval path. Because the current builder happens not to emit held financial_quality impacts, no normal-output leak was observed. But the durable validator does not enforce the claimed boundary, so future builder drift or hand-built reports can pass validation with a held-position financial_quality impact and bypass the intended later-slice review. This repeats the same class of guard-vs-claim gap previously found in Round5 trade-event privacy/scope reviews.

Required repair: tighten financial_quality guard ⑮ and tests. Acceptable repair: for `source_field=="financial_quality"`, require `visibility_shape=="candidate_row_impact"`, `impact_scope=="new_entry"`, `privacy_class=="public_tracked"`, and reject the impact when `machine.stateful_risk.position_state=="held"` (or any equivalent explicit candidate-only invariant). Keep the existing comparison-only checks: `field_class=="structured"`, `production_effect_enabled is False`, `veto_class=="none"`, `new_entry_effect in {"priority_down","informational","none"}`, `holding_effect=="none"`, and visible `风控触发` marker. Add an adversarial test that mutates a held report to include a financial_quality impact and proves the validator rejects it, plus positive coverage for the normal candidate red-flag landing.

Boundary: do not add live Tushare / provider calls; do not add new governance thresholds; do not make financial_quality production-effective; do not change EGS / TopN / selection / table action / share size / veto / S3b / broker behavior; do not turn this into holding financial-quality management; do not commit `research/results/a_short/iv_feed_20260605/iv_feed.json`.

OPEN P2 (2026-06-18): A-short 4.2 Round5 block_trade discount price coverage guard gap. Required ID `R-ASHORT-GAP42-ROUND5-BLOCK-TRADE-DISCOUNT-PRICE-COVERAGE-GUARD-GAP`; status `resolved` (Codex re-`审查 PASS` + committed master d98db25e 2026-06-18); severity `P2`; scope reviewed: `runners/a_short_weekly_pipeline.py`, `runners/a_short_m67_render.py`, `schemas/a_short_weekly_report.schema.json`, `tests/test_a_short_weekly_pipeline.py`, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`; design source reviewed: `C:\Users\cnhea\Desktop\4.2.md` decision 5 / 大宗交易折价率 requirement / comparison-only boundary; excluded untracked byproduct `research/results/a_short/iv_feed_20260605/iv_feed.json`; PIT label `A-short 4.2 Round5 / block_trade third cut / discount price evidence / field coverage / no-dangling`.

Finding: the discount direction is acceptable in purpose. The slice uses raw same-day close from `pro.daily`, keeps discount comparison-only, and does not change EGS / TopN / selection / action / share size / veto / production effect. The material gap is coverage/no-dangling on the block-trade price side. `_fetch_block_trade()` requests `price`, but it still treats a response missing the `price` column as a successful checked fetch and returns rows with `price=None`. `_block_trade_events()` then emits `parties[].price=None`; `_attach_block_discount()` can set `discount_status="checked"` and add event `close`, while every party has `discount=None`. `validate_weekly_report()` accepts this because checked discount days only require `close` and a `discount` key, not explicit `price` evidence. The schema also leaves `parties[].price` optional, so a hand-built checked discount event with no price key can pass schema and validator.

Materiality: 4.2 requires each new external field to prove availability / reliability before use, and discount cannot be computed from close alone. A checked discount layer with missing block-trade price can render as `—` while still presenting the discount slice as checked. This is not a production-trading leak because the field remains comparison-only, but it creates false coverage evidence for the third-cut field and can hide provider/API shape drift.

Required repair: tighten block_trade discount price coverage in the current working tree. Acceptable repair: (1) make `_fetch_block_trade()` fail closed when the `price` column is absent for the active discount slice, or add an explicit price/discount unknown path that does not mark discount checked when price evidence is unavailable; (2) for `discount_status="checked"` and non-`unchecked_discount_dates`, require every party to carry explicit `price` and `discount` keys, while `price=None` remains legal only when the provider column/key exists but the cell is blank/nonfinite; (3) reject checked discount events with missing party `price` key or missing party `discount` key; (4) add adversarial tests for missing `price` column, checked event missing party `price`, checked event missing party `discount`, plus a positive test for legal null price cell with the key present.

Boundary: do not run live Tushare unless the user says `执行`; do not add governance thresholds; do not make discount production-effective; do not create new `operation_impact`; do not change EGS / TopN / selection / table action / share size / price formulas / S3b / broker behavior; do not commit `research/results/a_short/iv_feed_20260605/iv_feed.json`.

OPEN P2 (2026-06-18): A-short 4.2 Round5 block_trade parties buyer/seller coverage guard gap. Required ID `R-ASHORT-GAP42-ROUND5-BLOCK-TRADE-PARTIES-COVERAGE-GUARD-GAP`; status `resolved` (Codex re-`审查 PASS` + committed master ece634c4 2026-06-18); severity `P2`; scope reviewed: `runners/a_short_weekly_pipeline.py`, `runners/a_short_m67_render.py`, `schemas/a_short_weekly_report.schema.json`, `tests/test_a_short_weekly_pipeline.py`, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`; design source reviewed: `C:\Users\cnhea\Desktop\4.2.md` decision 5 / §5.3 / §11.5 / §12.2 / §13; excluded untracked byproduct `research/results/a_short/iv_feed_20260605/iv_feed.json`; PIT label `A-short 4.2 Round5 / block_trade second cut / buyer-seller parties / field coverage / no-dangling`.

Finding: the block_trade parties direction is acceptable in purpose: buyer/seller is added as same-endpoint enrichment, stays inside `block_trade.events[].parties`, renders a comparison-only buyer→seller column/text, and does not change EGS / TopN / selection / table action / share size / veto / production effect. The gap is coverage/no-dangling. `_fetch_block_trade()` requests `buyer,seller` but only requires `ts_code` and `amount`; if the provider response lacks `buyer` / `seller` columns, it still returns a successful row with `buyer=None,seller=None`. `_block_trade_events()` then emits a checked event with parties `[{"buyer": null, "seller": null, ...}]`, and render / M6.7 text can show `?→?` while the report is still `status="checked"`. Separately, `schemas/a_short_weekly_report.schema.json` leaves `events[].parties` optional, and `validate_weekly_report()` / `validate_operation_impact_no_dangling()` accept a checked block_trade event with no `parties` at all. This contradicts the second-cut claim that buyer/seller parties are now the landed field.

Materiality: 4.2 requires each newly fetched data item to prove availability / quality before use, and every analysis field must have a real M6.7 landing or an explicit unknown path. The previous first-cut live note recorded `ts_code/trade_date/price/vol/amount`, not buyer/seller, so the current `SESSION_LOG` claim that buyer/seller was already seen by the first-cut probe is not supported by the durable log. This is not a production-trading leak because the field remains comparison-only, but it can falsely present the buyer/seller slice as checked when the actual buyer/seller fields are absent.

Required repair: tighten block_trade parties coverage in the current working tree. Acceptable repair: (1) make `_fetch_block_trade()` fail closed for the parties slice when `buyer` / `seller` columns are absent, or add an explicit parties coverage status / unknown path that does not render `?→?` as checked buyer/seller evidence; (2) enforce a write-time no-dangling rule for checked `block_trade.events`: if parties are part of the active second-cut schema, each event must carry `parties`, and `len(parties)` must match `trade_count`; each party must have explicit `buyer`, `seller`, and `amount` keys, while individual values may be null only when the provider column exists but the cell is blank; (3) add adversarial tests for missing buyer/seller columns, missing `parties`, and party-count mismatch, plus positive tests for legal parties and legal blank buyer/seller cells; (4) fix the top SESSION_LOG / comments claim so it does not say buyer/seller was verified in the first-cut live probe unless a separate user-approved `执行` actually verifies it.

OPEN P2 (2026-06-18): A-short 4.2 Round5 block_trade / dragon_list coverage and holding-privacy guard gap. Required ID `R-ASHORT-GAP42-ROUND5-TRADE-EVENT-COVERAGE-PRIVACY-GUARD-GAP`; status `resolved` (Codex re-`审查 PASS` + committed master 606bd225 2026-06-18); severity `P2`; scope reviewed: `runners/a_short_weekly_pipeline.py`, `runners/a_short_phase5_engine.py`, `runners/a_short_m67_render.py`, `schemas/a_short_weekly_report.schema.json`, `schemas/examples/a_short_gap_data_field_registry.example.json`, `tests/test_a_short_weekly_pipeline.py`, `tests/test_a_short_gap_data_registry.py`, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`; design source reviewed: `C:\Users\cnhea\Desktop\4.2.md` §5.3 / §10.3 / §11.5 / §12.2 / §13; excluded untracked byproduct `research/results/a_short/iv_feed_20260605/iv_feed.json`; PIT label `A-short 4.2 Round5 / block_trade first cut / dragon-list sibling guard / unknown-not-clear / holding privacy shape`.

Finding: the block_trade first-cut direction is acceptable in purpose: it stays analysis-only / comparison-only, uses gated `pro.block_trade`, writes a weekly `block_trade` section, lands row-level `block_trade_appearance` impacts, and does not change EGS / TopN / selection / action / sizing. However the write-time consumer guard is incomplete in the same class as the dragon-list guards it mirrors. Independent probes showed malformed reports are accepted: (1) `block_trade.status="checked"` with `window_dates=[]` and no events; (2) `block_trade.status="checked"` with every `window_dates` entry also in `unchecked_dates` and no events; (3) a held report with a `block_trade_appearance` impact mutated from `holding_row_impact/private_account` to `candidate_row_impact/public_tracked`; and the same three states are accepted for `dragon_list_appearance`. This means a report can claim a checked no-event state without any actually checked date, or carry a holding-related event impact with public/candidate shape, while `validate_weekly_report()` still passes. There is also active runner prose drift in the new block_trade comments/docstring that says non-candidate holdings are future work, while the actual implementation and registry claim the current slice covers `weekly.reports` (candidate plus account holdings).

Materiality: 4.2 requires unknown-not-clear for provider coverage and private handling for true account / holding information. The current builder normally emits the correct block_trade holding privacy shape, and `--account` output-path guard still protects normal private reports, so no tracked leak was observed. The material gap is the consumer/write-time contract: future builder drift or hand-constructed reports can pass validation with false coverage or public/candidate holding shape. This affects review quality and the final M6.7 artifact contract, especially because block_trade deliberately copied the dragon-list pattern and the sibling guard gap is already proven.

Required repair: tighten the trade-event write-time guard for both `block_trade` and sibling `dragon_list` in the current working tree. Acceptable repair:
(1) For each checked trade-event section, require `window_dates` to be non-empty and require at least one actually checked date (`window_dates - unchecked_dates` non-empty). A state where no dates were checked must be `unknown_or_unavailable`, not `checked`; reject checked-empty-window and checked-all-unchecked. Keep partial failure valid only when at least one date was checked.
(2) Enforce row privacy / visibility shape for trade-event impacts. If the report is a held position (`machine.stateful_risk.position_state == "held"`) and the impact source is `dragon_list_appearance` or `block_trade_appearance`, the impact must be `visibility_shape="holding_row_impact"`, `impact_scope="existing_holding"`, `new_entry_effect="none"`, and `privacy_class="private_account"` or stricter. Non-held rows must remain candidate/public shape. Do not rely only on registry tests.
(3) Add adversarial tests for block_trade and dragon_list: checked empty window rejected, checked all-unchecked rejected, held impact public/candidate mutation rejected, plus positive tests for a legal partial-unchecked state and a legal held private impact.
(4) Align active block_trade comments/docstrings with the actual current scope: first cut covers `weekly.reports` (candidate plus account holdings); buyer/seller seat analysis and discount-rate analysis are later, but non-candidate holding coverage is not later.

Boundary: do not change EGS / TopN / selection / table action / share size / price formulas / S3b / broker behavior; do not add governance thresholds; do not make dragon-list or block_trade production-effective; do not run live Tushare; do not change provider behavior except tests/guards needed for this Required; do not commit `research/results/a_short/iv_feed_20260605/iv_feed.json`.

OPEN P2 (2026-06-18): A-short 4.2 Round5 dragon-list third-cut holding registry privacy gap. Required ID `R-ASHORT-GAP42-ROUND5-DRAGON-HOLDING-REGISTRY-PRIVACY-GAP`; status `resolved` (Codex re-`审查 PASS` + committed master af8ff67e 2026-06-18); severity `P2`; scope reviewed: `runners/a_short_weekly_pipeline.py`, `runners/a_short_m67_render.py`, `schemas/examples/a_short_gap_data_field_registry.example.json`, `tests/test_a_short_weekly_pipeline.py`, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`; design source reviewed: `C:\Users\cnhea\Desktop\4.2.md` §5.1 / §10.3 / §11.5 / §12.2 / §13; excluded untracked byproduct `research/results/a_short/iv_feed_20260605/iv_feed.json`; PIT label `A-short 4.2 Round5 / dragon_list third cut / holding coverage / registry privacy consistency`.

Finding: the third-cut runtime direction is acceptable in the current working tree. Dragon-list coverage expands from candidates to `weekly["reports"]` (candidates plus account holdings), held rows receive `holding_row_impact` with `privacy_class="private_account"`, `_card_field()` unmasks the Tier-3 `板块资金事件` only when it contains the `龙虎榜对照` marker, and the existing dragon-list guard still keeps the source comparison-only (`production_effect_enabled=false`, `veto_class=none`, no sizing/action/blocked-add effect). The gap is the registry row. `schemas/examples/a_short_gap_data_field_registry.example.json::dragon_list_appearance` now says the field covers holdings and `operation_impact_target="both"`, but the same row still says `visibility_shape="candidate_row_impact"` and `privacy_class="public_tracked"`. Independent probe output: `operation_impact_target=both`, `visibility_shape=candidate_row_impact`, `privacy_class=public_tracked`, and `owner_mentions_holding=True`.

Materiality: 4.2 §10.3 requires anything involving real account / real holding information to route as private, and §12.2 requires advisory/display fields involving holdings to use the private path. The runtime path guard appears to protect `--account` outputs, so this is not an observed tracked-output leak. But the durable registry is the governance table future slices use for privacy and landing decisions. Leaving a holding-capable field marked `public_tracked` makes future review / commit decisions unsafe and repeats the same class of registry drift seen in earlier Round5 findings.

Required repair: align the registry with the actual third-cut scope and add a guard so it cannot regress. Acceptable repair: split the registry representation into candidate/public and holding/private rows, or use an equally explicit representation that does not leave a holding-capable `operation_impact_target=both` row marked only `candidate_row_impact` / `public_tracked`. The holding side must state `visibility_shape=holding_row_impact` and `privacy_class=private_account` (or stricter), with owner/ref/landing text matching the runtime `holding_row_impact` behavior. Add a focused registry test that fails if a row mentions account holdings / `holding_row_impact` / `private_account` behavior or has `operation_impact_target="both"` while still claiming only `public_tracked` or only `candidate_row_impact`. Keep the runtime comparison-only boundary unchanged unless a small wording update is necessary.

Boundary: do not change EGS/TopN/selection/action/share size/price formulas/S3b/broker behavior; do not add governance thresholds; do not make dragon-list or top_inst production-effective; do not run live Tushare; do not change provider behavior; do not commit `research/results/a_short/iv_feed_20260605/iv_feed.json`.
