OPEN P2 (2026-06-18): A-short 4.2 Round5 dragon-list top_inst seat coverage guard gap. Required ID `R-ASHORT-GAP42-ROUND5-DRAGON-SEATS-COVERAGE-GUARD-GAP`; status `resolved` (Codex re-`审查 PASS` + committed master 842e016e 2026-06-18); severity `P2`; scope reviewed: `runners/a_short_weekly_pipeline.py`, `runners/a_short_m67_render.py`, `schemas/a_short_weekly_report.schema.json`, `schemas/examples/a_short_gap_data_field_registry.example.json`, `tests/test_a_short_weekly_pipeline.py`, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`; design source reviewed: `C:\Users\cnhea\Desktop\4.2.md` decision 5 / §5.3 / §10 / §11.5 / §12.2 / §13; excluded untracked byproduct `research/results/a_short/iv_feed_20260605/iv_feed.json`; PIT label `A-short 4.2 Round5 / dragon_list top_inst seats / unknown-not-clear / seat evidence coverage`.

Finding: the second-cut direction is acceptable: `top_inst` stays comparison-only, does not create a new `operation_impact`, does not change EGS/TopN/selection/action/share size, and keeps true provider calls gated behind `--confirm`. The gap is the seat coverage contract. `validate_weekly_report()` only checks the forward case "if an event has `seats`, it must not be on an unchecked seat date"; it does not check the reverse case. Independent probes showed three malformed reports are accepted: (1) `dragon_list.seats_status="checked"` with an event that has no `seats` and no `unchecked_seat_dates`; (2) an event with `seats` but no `inst_net_buy`; (3) an event with `seats`/`inst_net_buy` but no `seats_status`. This lets the report claim the seat layer is checked while per-event seat evidence is missing or not governed by any coverage status. It violates 4.2's unknown-not-clear and no-dangling rules for new provider data.

Required repair: add a reverse seat coverage guard in `validate_weekly_report()` (or equivalent write-time guard). Acceptable invariant: if any event has `seats` or `inst_net_buy`, `dragon_list.seats_status` must be `checked`; if `seats_status=="checked"`, then every event whose `trade_date` is not in `unchecked_seat_dates` must carry a `seats` array and an explicit `inst_net_buy` key (value may be null); events on `unchecked_seat_dates` must not carry `seats`/`inst_net_buy`; if `seats_status=="unknown_or_unavailable"`, no event may carry `seats`/`inst_net_buy`; `unchecked_seat_dates` must stay inside `window_dates` and should only be meaningful with `seats_status=="checked"`. Add adversarial tests for all accepted bad cases above, plus positive tests for checked empty seats (`seats=[]`, `inst_net_buy=null`) and unchecked date without seats.

Boundary: do not add governance thresholds, do not make top_inst production-effective, do not create new action effects, do not change `operation_impact` guard ⑬ unless needed for wording only, do not change EGS/TopN/selection/table action/share size/price formulas/S3b/broker behavior, do not run live Tushare, and do not commit `research/results/a_short/iv_feed_20260605/iv_feed.json`.

OPEN P1 (2026-06-18): Tushare health probe plaintext token / false-health diagnostic gap. Required ID `R-TUSHARE-HEALTH-PROBE-PLAINTEXT-TOKEN-AND-FALSE-OK-GAP`; status `resolved` (Codex re-`审查 PASS` + committed master 695b8621 2026-06-18; 实测真探针 [OK] 确认 weekly pinned 取数正常); severity `P1`; scope reviewed: untracked `runners/tushare_health_probe.py`; related current weekly path: `runners/a_short_iv_feed_probe.py::init_tushare_pro`, `runners/a_short_weekly_pipeline.py`, `runners/materialize_execution_price_data_tushare.py`; excluded untracked byproduct `research/results/a_short/iv_feed_20260605/iv_feed.json`; PIT label `A-short infrastructure / Tushare health probe / token transport + false OK`.

Finding: the probe is useful in purpose, but unsafe and misleading as written. First, `_TUSHARE_HTTP_URL = "http://api.tushare.pro"` and the direct comparison posts `{"token": token, ...}` to that URL, so running the helper in a real environment can send `TUSHARE_TOKEN` over plaintext HTTP. Not printing the token is not enough; AGENTS security rules also forbid unsafe propagation of secrets. Second, package-path success is `bool(cols)`, so a response with columns but zero rows is treated as healthy. Finding 1 (row landing / no-dangling gap): desktop `4.2.md` lines 276-281, 345, 741, and 770 require forward events to be analysis-only but still land in M6.7 as candidate/holding row impact: candidates can get `manual_review` / `priority_down` / `sizing_down` / `observe_required`; holdings can get `hold_watch` / `blocked_add_required` / `reduce_review` text; M6.7 landing includes `upcoming_events`, `风控触发`, `操作建议`, and when applicable `股数`. The implementation only sets `weekly["upcoming_events"]` as a global weekly object (`runners/a_short_weekly_pipeline.py` around `_exdiv_codes` / `_upcoming_events`) and renders one global Markdown section (`runners/a_short_m67_render.py` upcoming-events block). It does not attach the event to the affected `reports[]` row, does not create row-level `operation_impact`, and does not update the affected row's user-visible `风控触发` / `操作建议`. Independent Codex probe injected a valid `limit_unlock` for `600000.SH`; `validate_weekly_report()` accepted the weekly report, but the 600000.SH row had `row_operation_impact_sources=[]`, no `upcoming_events` / `limit_unlock` / `解禁` text in the row, `风控触发=="无"`, and `操作=="建仓"`. Materiality: the calendar is visible as a side table but is disconnected from the exact M6.7 decision row the user reads, so the field is dangling for the row-level risk/action contract.

Required repair for Finding 1: preserve the global `upcoming_events` index if useful, but also consume each checked event into the affected candidate/holding row's M6.7 surface. Minimum acceptable behavior: candidate rows with near `limit_unlock` show a user-visible event warning and an analysis-only row impact (`manual_review` / `observe_required` / `priority_down` / `sizing_down` as the reviewed mapping chooses) without becoming a production hard veto; holding rows show holding-scope warning text such as `hold_watch` / `blocked_add_required` / `reduce_review` text only, with no automatic sell/reduce action before S3b. The repair must keep `production_effect_enabled=false`, must not change EGS selection, TopN, production `result/a_short`, historical backtest, broker/order behavior, or price formulas. Add adversarial tests proving a valid event is visible on the exact candidate row and on the exact holding row, not only in a global section.

Finding 2 (mandatory guard tests missing): `4.2.md` line 741 explicitly requires `row no-dangling`, `PIT observed_at`, `unknown-not-clear`, `no-EGS/TopN-change`, and `no-hard-veto-rescue` tests for the forward_events first version. The added `UpcomingEventsTests` cover builder PIT, unknown-vs-checked, schema/validator, renderer, and fetcher fail-closed, but they do not cover row no-dangling, do not assert the EGS/TopN/report row set/order is unchanged by injecting an unlock provider, and do not assert forward events cannot rescue or upgrade any hard-veto / production-veto path. Materiality: the same slice claims "analysis-only / 不改 EGS·TopN·动作", but the required safety contract is not test-pinned; a future refactor could either leave events dangling again or accidentally turn them into production action.

Required repair for Finding 2: add tests that (a) fail if an `upcoming_events` item does not land in the matching M6.7 row surface, (b) compare report row set/order and candidate behavior with/without injected unlock events to prove no EGS/TopN change, and (c) prove a hard-veto candidate remains hard-vetoed and is not rescued by any positive/neutral event, while an event warning cannot become `production_hard_veto` or write production evidence. Keep tests no-network via injected providers / fixtures only.

Claude self-discovered finding for A-short account-bearing weekly M6.7 output privacy leak vector (2026-06-16; status `resolved` (committed `155e3ad` local master 2026-06-16, Codex re-`审查 PASS` + user `提交`); severity `P1`; scope `runners/a_short_weekly_pipeline.py`, `runners/weekly_screening.ps1`, `.gitignore`, `tests/test_a_short_holdings_in_m67.py`, `docs/a_short_holdings_in_m67_design.md`; PIT label `A-short holdings-in-M6.7 / privacy / account output routing / git-leak surface`; Required ID `R-ASHORT-HOLDINGS-WEEKLY-ACCOUNT-OUTPUT-PRIVATE-ROUTING`): surfaced while running S1 with the user's real account. `runners/weekly_screening.ps1` hardcodes the M6.7 output to `research/results/a_short/<as_of>/weekly_m67.json`, a **git-tracked** lane (only `research/results/a_short/m67_validation_*/` is gitignored). A direct `a_short_weekly_pipeline.py --account ... --out <tracked path>` call (exactly the shape used in the S1 validation run) had the same exposure with no guard. Fix (this slice, 固化): (1) `.gitignore` add `state/*/weekly_private/` (scheme covers a_short/a_long/us_short/us_long); (2) `weekly_screening.ps1` routes `-Account` output to gitignored `state/a_short/weekly_private/<as_of>/`, observation-only stays at the standard research lane (committable evidence, no holdings); (3) pipeline hard guard `_reject_nonprivate_account_output_path` — `--account` + `--out` **inside repo and not git-ignored** → fail-fast `SystemExit` before any fetch/write; repo-external paths (temp/external drive) allowed (git can't commit them); `--allow-nonprivate-account-out` explicit override; (4) tests + design doc §8. Boundary: no change to `egs_main`/top-N/EGS scoring/engine action/semantic/observation-only routing/existing `_reject_production_output_path`. Verify: holdings + weekly pipeline tests **128 OK** (the ~25 existing `--account`+tmp-`--out` tests still pass because temp dirs are repo-external); guard unit tests cover inside-nonprivate-refuse / private-ok / outside-ok / no-account-ok / override-ok / main-fail-fast. Replaced the substring heuristic with **git ground truth** — new `_is_account_output_git_ignored()` runs `git -C <repo_root> check-ignore -q -- <out>`; guard refuses iff `--account` and out path is inside repo AND `git check-ignore` does NOT match (git unavailable/error → fail-closed = treat as not-ignored). Repo-external paths still early-return (allowed). Net: guard-accepted ⟺ (outside repo) OR (actually git-ignored), so fake/nested/case-variant `weekly_private` follow git's real per-platform decision. Codex review finding for A-short holdings-always-in-M6.7 S1 Tier-2 price clock drift (2026-06-15; status `resolved` (committed `3e81200` local master 2026-06-16, Codex `审查 PASS` + user `提交`); severity `P1`; scope `engine/a_short_egs_full_adapter.py`, `runners/a_short_weekly_pipeline.py`, `tests/test_a_short_holdings_in_m67.py`, current S1 design `docs/a_short_holdings_in_m67_design.md`; PIT label `A-short holdings-in-M6.7 / account_position_egs_full / price clock / current price`; Required ID `R-ASHORT-HOLDINGS-S1-TIER2-EGSFULL-CLOSE-PRICE-CLOCK-DRIFT`): the Tier-2 route correctly reuses the current `egs_full_<as_of>.csv` scoring row for an account holding that is outside top-N, but it also maps `egs_full.close` into `candidate.quote.close` and then `normalize_candidate()` uses that candidate quote as the M6.7 `close`, even though the S1 design requires actual M6.7 price to come from the weekly pipeline price clock. Independent probe reproduced the drift: with a Tier-2 holding whose `egs_full.close` was `999.0` and whose fetched/latest price series close was `10.25`, `_build_holdings()` produced normalized `close=999.0` while `price_series[-1].close=10.25`. Materiality: the row can display or calculate holding action/prices from a stale or mismatched CSV close while the lineage says the weekly price clock is fresh; this directly contaminates the final M6.7 holding row. Required repair: for `account_position_egs_full` rows, keep `egs_full` as score/risk lineage, but override the candidate/current close from the accepted `price_provider` latest bar (or override normalized `close`) before M6.7 report construction; do not let `egs_full.close` be the current-price authority. Add a regression where `egs_full.close` deliberately differs from the fetched price-series close and assert the normalized/report/table current price uses the weekly price-provider close. Boundary: do not change `egs_main`, top-N admission, EGS score semantics, semantic providers, broker/order behavior, or the S1 no-active-stop/no-active-add boundary. **Claude `修复` (2026-06-16)**: judged correct. `_build_holdings` now overrides `cand["quote"]["close"]` with the accepted `price_provider` latest bar (`series[-1]["close"]`) for **all** injected holdings before `normalize_candidate`, so `egs_full.close` is never the current-price authority; egs_full stays only as EGS score/risk lineage. Regression `tests/test_a_short_holdings_in_m67.py::BuildHoldingsTests::test_tier2_close_uses_price_clock_not_egsfull` (egs_full.close=999.0, fetched series close=10.25) asserts normalized `close==10.25` while `egs_score` still reuses egs_full (71.5). Verify: holdings+render+weekly+phase5 **187 OK**; no `egs_main`/top-N/semantic-provider/boundary change. **Codex re-`审查` PASS (2026-06-16)**: confirmed the working tree keeps current price on injected holdings from the accepted price-provider bar and not `egs_full.close`; targeted holdings test with local jsonschema stub 18 OK; py_compile OK. **Resolved at `3e81200`** (local master 2026-06-16, Codex `审查 PASS` + user `提交`).

A-short weekly M6.7 cninfo semantic provider bypasses the reviewed semantic-summary safety gates (status `resolved` — Codex `审查 PASS`, committed master 2026-06-13; severity `P2`; scope `runners/a_short_weekly_pipeline.py`, `runners/a_short_phase5_engine.py`, `tests/test_a_short_weekly_pipeline.py`, `docs/a_short_semantic_risk_coverage.md`; PIT label `A-short semantic-risk into M6.7 / Slice 1b cninfo provider / top15 and batch-quality contract`; Required ID `R-ASHORT-M67-CNINFO-PROVIDER-BYPASSES-SEMANTIC-SUMMARY-GATES`): the new direct `_build_cninfo_semantic_provider` is directionally useful, but it re-implements the semantic layer instead of reusing the already reviewed summary contract. Codex probes show it fetches every `weekly_candidates` item, not the semantic layer's main-board Top15 watch pool, so non-mainboard / outside-cap symbols can be requested and fed into M6.7 despite the established bounded semantic-risk boundary. It also converts a batch of 15 `ok=True` / empty-announcement cninfo rows into per-stock `clear`, bypassing `build_summary_from_fetches`' batch-empty / batch-unhealthy gate that downgrades mass-empty cninfo windows to `unknown` rather than "checked clear". A negative lookback is accepted and passed to the fetcher, which can invert the date window and produce the same false-clear signature. Malformed rows lacking `ts_code` are inserted under a `"None"` key instead of being treated as provider-quality failure for the requested candidate set. This creates the exact old risk class: a provider outage, anti-scrape empty batch, bad lookback, or malformed response can become `semantic_risk.status=clear` inside M6.7 instead of `unknown`, silently removing a semantic warning path. Required repair: centralize the weekly cninfo provider through the existing semantic summary contract or faithfully reuse its gates. Minimum: derive the semantic fetch universe with `main_board_top15(weekly_candidates)` (or the same shared helper) and do not fetch/feed non-mainboard or outside-Top15 names; validate `--cninfo-lookback-days` as a positive integer before any fetch; treat missing/malformed rows for requested codes as `unknown`, not clear, and never create a `"None"` code mapping; apply the same batch-empty / batch-unhealthy rule used by `build_summary_from_fetches` so a 15-name ok-empty batch cannot produce all-clear M6.7 semantic state. Add adversarial tests for mass-empty Top15 -> unknown, partial/missing requested code -> unknown, non-main/outside-Top15 not requested/fed, zero/negative lookback rejected or routed to unknown without clear, malformed raw row no `"None"` mapping, and happy-path official risk still feeds M6.7. Boundary: weekly semantic provider integration + tests/docs only; no DeepSeek, no production EGS ranking/scoring, no historical backtest, no real network call in tests, no V14.2 spec change. **Working-tree repaired (Claude `修复` 2026-06-13)**: `_build_cninfo_semantic_provider` rewritten to REUSE `build_summary_from_fetches` (the reviewed contract) instead of a thin re-impl — it now derives the universe via `main_board_top15(codes)` (non-mainboard/outside-Top15 neither fetched nor fed), drops malformed/no-`ts_code` rows (no `"None"` mapping; requested-code-missing → `not_fetched` → `unknown`), and inherits the batch-empty/unhealthy gate (mass ok-empty → `unknown`, never all-clear). `--cninfo-lookback-days` validated as positive int before any fetch (else `None`, no fetch, no false-clear). Adversarial tests added (mass-empty→unknown, missing code→unknown, ChiNext not-fetched/not-fed, zero/negative/non-int lookback rejected without fetch, malformed-row no `"None"`, genuine official risk still feeds). Resolved on Codex re-`审查` PASS + `提交`.

CURRENT MECHANISM (final — narrowest strategy):
- `RISK_KEYWORD_MAP` carries `severity` (high 立案/处罚/ST · medium 监管函件/关注/资金占用/担保 · low 诉讼/仲裁); official_structured events carry `severity` (schema enum high/medium/low).
- `_is_routine_occupation_report` suppresses a fund_occupation match ONLY when the title is a routine disclosure form (`ROUTINE_OCCUPATION_FORMS` = 专项说明/专项审核/汇总表) AND carries an explicit no-occupation negation (`NO_OCCUPATION_NEGATIONS` = 不存在/未发生/未形成/无新增/无占用/…). high severity is never suppressed.
- Everything else → risk for the 2b-ii skill to downgrade: a bare routine report WITHOUT an explicit negation (incl. the exact 浦发 专项说明 / 关联资金往来情况汇总表) surfaces as `risk[medium]`; explicit/suspected occupation (存在/发生/被…占用) and 整改/违规担保/问询/立案/处罚 → risk. **Property: residual errors are false-positives only (skill downgrades), never 漏报** (a missed negation word merely shows one no-occupation report as risk — harmless). Tested both ways (`test_only_routine_form_WITH_negation_is_suppressed` clears 不存在/未发生/无新增/不存在被…占用; `test_bare_routine_without_negation_now_surfaces_as_risk` + `test_explicit_or_suspected_occupation_surfaces_as_risk`).
- `render_semantic_risk_panel(summary)`: pure M6.7/weekly-visible markdown block (advisory/non-reproducible labels, coverage, lists only flagged risk/unknown/needs-review candidates with official severity+latest-date + web_llm cell + 需人工复核, clear summarized; never mixed into deterministic reports). Panel WIRING into the weekly pipeline deferred (render function only here).

SUPERSEDED interim (do NOT re-introduce): rounds 1-3 used a blanket `NEGATIVE_PATTERNS` then an `_has_adverse_marker`/`ESCALATION_MARKERS` override — both DELETED; they caused 漏报 on negated forms (未发生/无新增/不存在被…占用) across a 5-round whack-a-mole, hence the narrowest inversion above. The pre-calibration artifact `research/results/a_short/semantic_risk_summary_20260612.json` (old shape, no `severity`) was DELETED.

A-short semantic-risk provider probe reports provider-quality-invalid cninfo rows as `clear_light` (status `resolved` Claude `修复` + Codex PASS + committed local master 2026-06-12; severity `P2`; scope `runners/a_short_semantic_risk_probe.py`, `tests/test_a_short_semantic_risk_probe.py`, `schemas/a_short_semantic_risk_probe_summary.schema.json` if status enum is extended, `docs/README.md`; PIT label `A-short semantic-risk Slice-1 / per-code status semantics / unknown-not-clear`; Required ID `R-ASHORT-SEMANTIC-PROBE-CNINFO-BAD-ROW-CLEAR-STATUS`): the P1 feasibility bypass is repaired, but `classify_cninfo_code` still sets `status="clear_light"` whenever `ok=True` and there is no PIT-valid announcement, even if the provider returned future-dated rows, unparseable disclosure dates, or non-dict malformed rows. Codex synthetic no-network probes after the latest repair show `future`, `bad_date`, and `bad_shape` samples now correctly produce `feasible=false` and reject forged `feasible=true`, but the affected per-code object still reports `status='clear_light'` with `dates_pit_ok=false` and one of `n_future_dated` / `n_unparseable_dates` / `n_bad_shape` > 0. That is not "successfully checked and clear"; it is an unknown / provider-quality-invalid state and contradicts the design/route wording that failure/unknown must not be disguised as clear. The same semantic hole can exist for PIT rows whose required fields or `secCode` mapping fail: feasibility blocks, but the per-code status can still read `clear_light`. Required repair: define and enforce status semantics so `clear_light` is allowed only for a genuinely successful clear result (empty successful window, or PIT-clean non-risk rows with required fields and mapping valid). Any code with future rows, unparseable dates, malformed rows, missing required fields, or code-mapping mismatch must be `unknown` or a formally added invalid-status enum. If using `unknown`, update `_check_provider_counts` so `ok=True` provider-quality failures may be `unknown`, while transport failures still must be `unknown`. Add adversarial tests for future-only, unparseable-only, non-dict-only, missing-field, and mapping-mismatch rows not being `clear_light`, plus a consistency test that a summary containing such an invalid row labelled `clear_light` raises. No real provider fetch or production behavior is authorized by this finding. **Working-tree repaired (Claude `修复` 2026-06-12, reused `unknown`)**: `classify_cninfo_code` now computes `quality_ok = (no future/unparseable/non-dict defects AND n_pit>0 AND required_fields_ok AND code_mapping_ok)` and assigns `status` as: not ok → `unknown`; ok + empty window → `clear_light`; ok + not quality_ok → `unknown`; ok + quality_ok + risk-keyword → `risk_candidate`; else `clear_light`. So future/unparseable/non-dict/missing-field/mapping-mismatch codes now read `unknown`, never `clear`. `_check_provider_counts` relaxed: the strict `ok ⇔ not-unknown` invariant became `not ok ⇒ unknown` (transport failure) for both providers + a cninfo per-code status-quality invariant (clear_light/risk_candidate require ok + clean + valid fields/mapping; risk_candidate requires PIT rows) while sina keeps `ok ⇒ not unknown`. Adversarial tests added (future / unparseable / non-dict / missing-field / mapping-mismatch → status `unknown`; + consistency test that a defective row labelled `clear_light` raises). Status enum unchanged (reused `unknown`); 44 tests pass; schema meta + py_compile OK. Resolved: Codex re-`审查` PASS + committed local master 2026-06-12.

A-short semantic-risk provider probe ignores unparseable / malformed cninfo returned rows in feasibility gate (status `resolved` Claude `修复` + Codex PASS + committed local master 2026-06-12; severity `P1`; scope `runners/a_short_semantic_risk_probe.py`, `tests/test_a_short_semantic_risk_probe.py`, `schemas/a_short_semantic_risk_probe_summary.schema.json` if fields are added; PIT label `A-short semantic-risk Slice-1 / cninfo provider-shape and disclosure-date gate`; Required ID `R-ASHORT-SEMANTIC-PROBE-CNINFO-BAD-DATE-SHAPE-BYPASS`): the future-date PIT leak was repaired, but returned rows with bad shape can still bypass feasibility. `classify_cninfo_code` filters `announcements` to dict rows before counting `n_returned`, so non-dict provider rows vanish completely. Rows with unparseable `announcementTime` set per-code `dates_pit_ok=False`, but because they yield `n_announcements=0`, they are excluded from the aggregate `announced` set and do not affect `n_dates_pit_ok`; a sample with 4 clean PIT-announced codes plus one unparseable-date returned row still produced `feasible=True`, no blocking reasons, and that bad-date code status `clear_light`. A sample with 4 clean PIT-announced codes plus one non-dict announcement row also produced `feasible=True` after silently treating the malformed row as no return. This violates the Slice-1 goal of proving cninfo field/date shape before Slice 2. Required repair: count raw returned items before filtering, expose and gate invalid returned rows (`n_unparseable_date_codes` / `n_bad_shape_codes` or equivalent), and ensure non-dict rows or unparseable disclosure dates cannot be reported as clean and cannot coexist with `feasible=True`. Add adversarial tests for unparseable dates, non-dict announcement rows, and mixed clean+bad-shape samples; keep the future-date PIT tests passing. No real provider fetch or production behavior is authorized by this finding. **Working-tree repaired (Claude `修复` 2026-06-12)**: `classify_cninfo_code` now counts `n_returned` on the RAW provider list BEFORE any `isinstance` filter, and partitions every returned row exactly into `n_announcements`(PIT dict+canonical+≤as_of) + `n_future_dated` + `n_unparseable_dates`(dict, bad/missing date) + `n_bad_shape`(non-dict), with a consistency assert that the four sum to `n_returned`; non-dict rows are no longer silently dropped. Three provider quality gates (`n_future_dated_codes==0`, `n_unparseable_date_codes==0`, `n_bad_shape_codes==0`) are now feasibility AND consistency conditions, so a malformed/unparseable/future row can neither be reported clean (`dates_pit_ok` == "all returned rows clean") nor coexist with `feasible=true`. Adversarial tests added: unparseable-date row counted-not-dropped, non-dict row counted-not-dropped, partition-sums-to-n_returned, and the exact Codex repros (4 clean + 1 unparseable-date code → feasible=false + reason; 4 clean + 1 non-dict-row code → feasible=false + reason). 43 tests pass; schema + consistency updated. Resolved: Codex re-`审查` PASS + committed local master 2026-06-12.

A-short semantic-risk provider probe accepts future-dated cninfo disclosures as PIT-valid (status `resolved` Claude `修复` + Codex PASS + committed local master 2026-06-12; severity `P1`; scope `runners/a_short_semantic_risk_probe.py`, `tests/test_a_short_semantic_risk_probe.py`, `schemas/a_short_semantic_risk_probe_summary.schema.json` if fields are added; PIT label `A-short semantic-risk Slice-1 / cninfo PIT disclosure-date gate`; Required ID `R-ASHORT-SEMANTIC-PROBE-CNINFO-FUTURE-DATE-PIT-LEAK`): `classify_cninfo_code(raw, as_of)` receives `as_of` but only checks that `announcementTime` is parseable; it does not verify parsed disclosure dates are `<= as_of`, and `fetch_cninfo` passes provider announcements through without a PIT cap. Adversarial tests added: future canonical string, future epoch-ms, future regulator-keyword row (cannot be `risk_candidate`), mixed past/future, and the exact Codex 4×future-only repro (now `feasible=false`, `n_announced=0`, `n_future_dated_codes=4`). 38 tests pass; schema + consistency updated. Resolved: Codex re-`审查` PASS + committed local master 2026-06-12.

A-short semantic-risk layer ↔ production reconciliation — RESOLVED via Slice 3 reconciliation (status `resolved` 2026-06-20, was `deferred-open` 2026-06-12; severity `P2`; scope `A-EGS/egs_main.py::stage3_ai_clearing`, the future semantic-risk advisory layer, `docs/a_short_semantic_risk_top15_enrichment_design_20260612.md` §1/§8 Slice 3; PIT label `A-short semantic-risk production integration / legacy-conflict / anti-forget`): the semantic-risk Top15 advisory layer is deliberately **isolated** from production `egs_main` for now (de-risk production, isolate scrape-grade providers, avoid touching the legacy LLM hard-veto, cheap iteration). Isolation is **staged, not permanent**. **[以下「Two debts remain OPEN」为历史 deferred 叙述,已 SUPERSEDED —— 见本条末 CLOSURE(Slice 3 已 land 2026-06-20:POL-RISK 移除 / cninfo 降 advisory)]** Two debts remain OPEN and must NOT be silently dropped: **(1) DeepSeek `POL-RISK-VETO` legacy-conflict** — production stage3 already does an LLM(DeepSeek)+web → industry hard-veto, which contradicts the new "web/LLM advisory-only, never hard-veto" principle; it is left untouched for now and must be explicitly reconciled (migrate to advisory, or re-govern as a reviewed deterministic veto). **(2) cninfo duplication / divergence** — stage3 has its own cninfo regulatory check (4 keywords, `cninfo_flag`) while the new layer will run an extended cninfo PIT check; two parallel cninfo paths can drift in keywords/caliber. Closure condition: ONLY after the advisory layer (Slice 2) is built + validated, run **Slice 3 (deterministic promotion)** — reconcile/unify the cninfo paths and decide the DeepSeek path's fate via a reviewed analyzer + governance + schema + PIT/forward-evidence slice. Until Slice 3 lands, this entry stays open as the standing anti-forget tracker. **CI-guard (LANDED with Slice 2a, `tests/test_semantic_risk_slice3_guard.py`)**: a **tracker-present anti-forget guard** — once advisory-layer code exists (`runners/a_short_semantic_risk_summary.py`), the test asserts THIS reconciliation tracker is still present in the register (carries the `DEFERRED, DO NOT CLOSE` marker AND still names Slice 3 / POL-RISK-VETO / cninfo); it FAILS only if the tracker is silently deleted/degraded. **Deliberate interpretation (NOT the literal "fail until reconciliation closed")**: a fail-until-closed guard would build-block the very staged delivery this same design mandates (Slice 3 comes AFTER the advisory layer is built+validated). So the guard ensures Slice 3 is not FORGOTTEN, not that it is done first; it does NOT block Slice 2a/2b commits. When Slice 3 actually lands it flips this tracker to `resolved` and updates/retires the guard. (Design §8 + this entry + the test docstring are aligned on this reading.) **CLOSURE (Slice 3, 2026-06-20, user-directed)**: 此前的 deferred-no-production-change 状态已被 superseded —— `POL-RISK-VETO` + 其 prompt-injection helpers 从 `egs_main.stage3_ai_clearing` **整段移除**(web/LLM 绝不自动生产硬否决);cninfo 监管检查**降为 advisory-only**(不再删生产候选,仅写 `cninfo_flag` 进 M6.7)+ 修 200-empty 假清白(空公告→`未核查` 非 `通过`);dead LLM-prompt-guard 测试(`tests/phase6/test_egs_main_llm_prompt_guard.py`,测已移除的 POL-RISK prompt)移除;`tests/test_semantic_risk_slice3_guard.py` 由 tracker-present anti-forget 重写为 stays-resolved 回归(禁 POL-RISK 代码符号复活 + cninfo 须 advisory)。真正的生产监管硬否决 = 另开 opt-in slice(b:修请求形态 `code,orgId` + PIT + governance + 测)。full detail 见 Hot Queue 顶部 2026-06-20 Slice-3 Required 条目。

A-short V14.3 slice 2b-impl ②a existing forward-return PIT/conflict bypass (status `resolved` committed local master 2026-06-11; finding Codex deeper re-`审查` FAIL 2026-06-11; severity `P1`; scope `engine/a_short_regime_comparison.py`, `tests/test_a_short_regime_comparison.py`; PIT label `comparison-only forward-return backfill / evidence-clock existing-value audit`; Required ID `R-V143-SLICE2B-COMPARISON-EXISTING-FWD-RETURN-PIT-CONFLICT-BYPASS`): `backfill_forward_returns` preserves every existing non-null horizon (`continue`) and then only validates shape/finite-ness, so prefilled values can bypass both the no-look-ahead check and the const-pinned CSI1000 return-basis check. For every existing non-null horizon, if the target trading day is not available under `as_of_now`, raise; if target is available, recompute the const-pinned CSI1000 return and raise on mismatch beyond a tight deterministic tolerance. A-short V14.3 slice 2b-impl ① partial `stk_limit` coverage silently treated as complete (status `resolved` Codex PASS + committed local master 2026-06-11; finding 2026-06-11 Codex `审查` FAIL; severity `P1`; scope `engine/a_short_regime_features.py`, `tests/test_a_short_regime_features.py`; PIT label `comparison-only regime daily-feature producer / limit breadth integrity`; Required ID `R-V143-SLICE2B-FEATURES-PARTIAL-STK-LIMIT-SILENT`): `_limit_sets` inner-joins `daily_day` to `stk_limit` and returns `have_limit=True` as soon as any matched stock exists. `compute_regime_daily_features` only flags `stk_limit_missing` when the entire day has no usable limit rows. Therefore a partial `stk_limit` panel (for example 2 daily stocks but only 1 limit row) emits `limit_up_count=1` with no limit-data quality flag, passes schema, and has no ledger semantic error. The public contract says `validate_ledger` enforces sorted/contiguous/PIT rows and that `merge_rows` / `plan_append` are PIT-capped at `as_of`; however independent probes found: `merge_rows([row("20240108")], [], "20240105")` accepts an already-existing future row; `plan_append(["20240108"], "20240105", calendar)` returns `[]`, treating the future-contaminated ledger as current; `validate_ledger(build_ledger(rows_through_20240108), trade_calendar=calendar)` passes because `validate_ledger` has no `as_of`; and a gappy ledger passes `validate_ledger(ledger)` when `trade_calendar` is omitted. Required repair: make the full ledger validation API require the run `as_of` and trading calendar (or split schema-only validation from a mandatory full gate), reject any existing or new row dated `> as_of`, reject future-contaminated existing ledgers in `merge_rows` / `plan_append` or require a validated ledger before planning, and add adversarial tests for existing-future rows, `plan_append` with future existing dates, validate-with-as_of future rows, and gappy-ledger-without-calendar acceptance. Keep the slice boundary unchanged: no data fetch, no EGS wiring, no file write, no production. **Repair (Claude `修复` 2026-06-11, working tree; closure requires Codex re-`审查` PASS + commit):** split `validate_ledger_envelope` (context-free schema/sorted/coverage/policy/boundary/per-row, explicitly NOT a substitute gate) from the sanctioned `validate_ledger(ledger, *, as_of, trade_calendar)` whose `as_of` + `trade_calendar` are now **mandatory** (omitting → TypeError) and which rejects any row dated `> as_of` (PIT) and any gap/non-subset vs the calendar (contiguity). `plan_append` now raises on a future-contaminated ledger (`max(existing) > as_of`) instead of returning `[]`; `merge_rows` now rejects existing rows dated `> as_of` as well as new ones. Added 5 adversarial tests (existing-future merge, future-contaminated plan_append, validate-with-as_of future row, mandatory-as_of/calendar TypeError, envelope-accepts-but-full-gate-rejects gap). Boundary unchanged. Verification: `tests.test_a_short_regime_ledger` 28/28 (+5) + full V14.3 + route-doc = 102/102 OK.

### SR-RESOURCE-001 - DataHub broad jobs lack code-level local resource budget enforcement

- Severity: P2
- Status: resolved
- Owner phase: Phase 7c DataHub / local execution stability
- Evidence: `docs/datahub_design.md` accepts a future shared DataHub for four subsystems, but before this reviewed slice there was no contract requiring slice-first local execution, partitioned reads, lazy materialization, incremental cache reuse, checkpoint / resume, or explicit user approval before all-market / all-lane / full-refresh jobs.
- Accepted calibration: this is not proof that the user's machine cannot run the system. The intended operating mode does not require all four systems to run at once. The risk is future implementation drift: a DataHub or runner slice could accidentally make full-system refresh the default and overload local execution or make review / debugging unstable.
- Mitigation evidence: reviewed slices add `schemas/datahub_local_resource_budget.schema.json`, `docs/datahub_local_resource_budget_contract_20260602.json`, `schemas/datahub_job_spec.schema.json`, and `schemas/examples/datahub_job_spec.example.json`, and route them through `docs/datahub_design.md`, `docs/README.md`, `docs/CURRENT.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and the Phase 7 handoff. ### SR-DATA-001 - Suspend inference can silently drop tradable stocks on partial daily response

- Severity: P1
- Status: resolved
- Owner phase: A-short weekly operation / Phase 6b maintenance
- Evidence: `A-EGS/egs_main.py:get_suspend_info` computes `suspended = all_codes - traded_codes` from single-day `pro.daily` responses and later `filter_l0` removes that set from candidates. There is no row-count / completeness sanity check before treating missing `daily` rows as suspended stocks.
- Accepted calibration: this is a real wrong-output path, but the trigger is a partial `pro.daily` bulk response. Frequency is not proven and is expected to be low; impact is silent and high when it fires. It does not block corrected 5d revalidation if that revalidation uses frozen historical generated cohorts and does not rerun `A-EGS/egs_main.py`.
- Required next action: resolved for the suspend-inference path. No further action is required for `SR-DATA-001` unless the suspend source / daily completeness policy is redesigned.
- Closure evidence: the reviewed change set updates `A-EGS/egs_main.py:get_suspend_info` to validate non-empty `pro.daily` payloads against `suspend_daily_min_coverage = 0.95` before inferring `suspended = all_codes - traded_codes`; below-threshold partial responses now raise instead of silently filtering candidates. The suspend cache key is bumped to `suspend_<date>_v2` so old unvalidated suspend-inference caches are not reused.
- Verification: `tests.phase6.test_egs_main_suspend_guard` covers partial daily rejection, valid high-coverage daily inference, cache-key v2 save behavior, and the existing all-empty daily fallback that skips suspend filtering rather than marking the whole market suspended.

### SR-DATA-004 - Suspend daily completeness threshold may false-fail on large-scale suspension days

- Severity: P3
- Status: open
- Owner phase: A-short weekly operation / Phase 6b maintenance
- Evidence: `SR-DATA-001` resolved the partial-`daily` silent drop path by requiring non-empty `pro.daily` payload coverage to meet `suspend_daily_min_coverage = 0.95`. Claude review accepted the fail-safe behavior but noted the threshold assumes normal-day suspensions stay below 5%; rare market-stress days with unusually broad suspensions could push true traded-code coverage below 95% and abort the run even when the provider response is complete.
- Accepted calibration: this is a low-risk operational watch item, not evidence that normal weekly runs are broken. A clear abort is safer than silently inferring missing rows as suspended stocks, and `suspend_daily_min_coverage` is already a configurable threshold.
- Mitigation evidence: the current observability slice makes `A-EGS/egs_main.py:get_suspend_info` write `logs/suspend_daily_coverage_<asof>.json` on pass, low-coverage fail, cache-hit, and no-daily skip paths; schema-validated `data_health` v1.2.0 `metrics.suspend_daily_coverage` mirrors the same latest observation. This does not close the watch item because no real weekly run has been reviewed yet.
- Required next action: monitor the first real weekly runs' `logs/suspend_daily_coverage_<asof>.json` and `data_health.metrics.suspend_daily_coverage`; if legitimate market-wide suspension conditions trip the threshold, tune the threshold or add a reviewed calendar / incident override with a focused regression test.

- Verification: `tests.phase6.test_forward_tracker_cache_guard` covers same-directory temp-file naming, one atomic replace call, sorted schema-column output, cleanup of the temp path after success, and preservation of the existing tracker when CSV serialization fails. `python -m unittest discover -s tests\phase6 -v` passed with 25 tests.

The former get-daily-all log that promised neutral defaults now states that downstream stat computation will abort.

### SR-EXEC-003 - Execution drawdown misses open-position mark-to-market

- Severity: P1
- Status: resolved
- Owner phase: Phase 5 execution backtest / ship-gate readiness
- Evidence: `runners/backtest_execution.py:simulate_execution` initializes `daily_equity` with `market_value = 0`, appends equity points only around realized exit events, and computes `max_drawdown` from realized cash-only equity. Open-position mark-to-market drawdown is not represented.
- Accepted calibration: current ship-gate status remains default-deny / not-evaluable because other required metrics are missing; the risk is future execution or ship-gate evidence overreading a realized-only drawdown.
- Closure: current execution reports publish `metrics.max_drawdown = null`, and `ship_gate_evaluation.metric_results.max_drawdown.value/passed = null` with an explicit mark-to-market not-evaluable reason. `daily_equity.csv` may still contain realized exit-date cash drawdown diagnostics, but those diagnostics are not used as ship-gate drawdown evidence.
- Verification: `tests.execution.test_backtest_execution` covers the time-stop and multi-trade paths with null drawdown evidence until mark-to-market equity exists.
- Required next action: no active SR-EXEC-003 action. If daily mark-to-market equity is later implemented, add reviewed tests before re-enabling numeric execution drawdown evidence.

### SR-EXEC-004 - Execution assumptions report cooldown / circuit breaker controls that are not simulated

- Severity: P1
- Status: resolved
- Owner phase: Phase 5 execution backtest / Phase 8 monitoring
- Evidence: `runners/backtest_execution.py:build_execution_assumptions` reports cooldown and portfolio circuit breaker controls as enabled, while the simulation loop does not enforce those controls.
- Accepted calibration: this is primarily an evidence overclaim / report-contract defect. It does not currently authorize full-size use, but it must be fixed before execution evidence is cited as if these controls were tested.
- Closure: current execution reports set `portfolio_circuit_breaker.enabled = false`, `new_entries_blocked = false`, `existing_positions_action = not_implemented`, and `cooldown.enabled = false`. The declared event-code coverage no longer includes `circuit_breaker` or `cooldown_block`, and report limitations state these controls are not simulated or safety evidence.
- Verification: `tests.execution.test_backtest_execution` covers the generated assumptions and limitations for unimplemented circuit breaker / cooldown controls while preserving schema-valid report output.
- Required next action: no active SR-EXEC-004 action. If these controls are later implemented, add reviewed simulator behavior and event-log tests before reporting them as enabled.

### SR-EXEC-005 - Zero-trade execution reports are aggregated as 0.0% monthly returns

- Severity: P1
- Status: resolved
- Owner phase: Phase 5 execution aggregation / ship-gate readiness
- Evidence: `runners/aggregate_execution_reports.py:report_total_return_for_aggregation` returns `0.0` for zero-trade reports when total return is absent, causing those months to enter monthly return, t-stat, and Sharpe calculations as flat observations.
- Accepted calibration: this does not currently pass the full ship gate because other metrics remain missing / not-evaluable; it can still inflate sample count or compress variance when execution evidence is later summarized.
- Closure evidence: the reviewed change set updates `runners/aggregate_execution_reports.py:report_total_return_for_aggregation` so zero-trade reports with null `metrics.total_return` remain missing / not evaluable for return statistics instead of being imputed as `0.0`. The monthly series, `monthly_return_count`, total-return mean, alpha t-stat, and Sharpe now consume only reports with an explicit numeric `total_return`. The aggregate report contract is bumped to `execution_aggregate_report` v1.1.1 and states the corrected zero-trade semantics.
- Verification: `tests.execution.test_aggregate_execution_reports` reverses the old zero-trade invariant: an input month with `trade_count = 0` and null `total_return` remains in input `month_count` but is excluded from `monthly_return_series` / `monthly_return_count` / `total_return_mean`. `tests.schema.test_execution_aggregate_report_schema` validates v1.1.1 and its zero-trade exclusion description.
- Required next action: no active `SR-EXEC-005` action. If a future reviewed cash-return model emits an explicit numeric return for zero-trade reports, add tests before allowing those observations into return statistics.

### SR-EXEC-006 - Execution aggregate can turn smoke / unbound forward-month inputs into full-size permission

- Severity: P1
- Status: resolved
- Owner phase: Phase 5 execution aggregation / ship-gate evidence integrity
- Evidence: `runners/aggregate_execution_reports.py:validate_compatible_reports` only checks that reports share the same `capital_context` summary and `mode`; it does not require `mode == production` for ship-gate permission. `--forward-live-months` is a plain CLI integer with no reviewed forward-tracking evidence artifact / ref binding. `build_ship_gate_evaluation` sets `full_size_allowed = status == "pass"`, and current tests include `tests/execution/test_aggregate_execution_reports.py:test_aggregate_with_benchmark_and_forward_months_can_pass_gate`, which can assert `full_size_allowed == true` from two default smoke reports plus a bare `--forward-live-months 12`.
- Accepted calibration: there is no broker or automatic order path, and current burst research is blocked before execution evidence is used. The risk is evidence / manual-sizing overclaim: the core `>= 12 months forward live` ship-gate requirement can be bypassed by an unbound CLI value, and smoke diagnostics can be presented as full-size manual-use permission.
- Closure evidence: the reviewed change set updates `runners/aggregate_execution_reports.py` so `execution_aggregate_report` v1.1.0 reads a reviewed `--forward-live-evidence-ref` JSON, validates `review_status='reviewed'`, derives / checks `forward_live_months` from that artifact, and keeps bare `--forward-live-months` diagnostic. The original smoke / bare-forward-month bypass is closed: smoke aggregates remain `not_evaluable` for ship-gate permission even if their numeric diagnostics pass, and bare CLI months cannot satisfy the forward-live metric. The later `SR-EXEC-007` closure further keeps `full_size_allowed` false until capacity / concurrency-adjusted returns are evaluable.
- Verification: `tests.execution.test_aggregate_execution_reports` now reverses the old smoke / bare-forward-month pass invariant, covers production reports without reviewed forward evidence staying `not_evaluable`, covers smoke reports with reviewed evidence staying `not_evaluable`, covers reviewed-evidence month matching, and rejects CLI / evidence month mismatches. `tests.schema.test_execution_aggregate_report_schema` validates the v1.1.0+ schema and required `forward_live_evidence_source` field.

### SR-EXEC-007 - Execution simulator serializes overlapping candidates and reuses bucket cash

- Severity: P2
- Status: resolved
- Owner phase: Phase 5 execution simulator / capacity and concurrency modeling
- Evidence: `runners/backtest_execution.py:simulate_execution` loops candidates sequentially. For each candidate it enters, subtracts cash, computes the full exit inside the same iteration, and adds cash back before the next candidate is sized. `calculate_shares` therefore sees cash after the prior candidate has already been closed, even when real holding windows would overlap. The code discloses "does not yet model concurrent open positions" in `limitations`, but there is no durable register gate for the resulting capacity / return distortion.
- Accepted calibration: this is distinct from `SR-CAP-001` bucket-ceiling validation. The risk is concurrency and cash-lock modeling: overlapping trades can reuse the same bucket capital serially, overstating capacity-adjusted returns if execution results are later used as ship-gate-like evidence.
- Closure evidence: the reviewed change set updates `runners/aggregate_execution_reports.py` and `schemas/execution_aggregate_report.schema.json` to v1.1.2. Aggregates still publish serialized execution return diagnostics, but `ship_gate_evaluation.status` remains `not_evaluable` and `full_size_allowed` remains false because capacity / concurrency-adjusted returns are not evaluable while input reports come from the serialized Phase 5 simulator. Production-mode reports with benchmark, reviewed forward-live evidence, and otherwise passing numeric diagnostics no longer unlock full-size permission.
- Verification: `tests.execution.test_aggregate_execution_reports` reverses the prior production + reviewed-forward-evidence pass path: monthly alpha, Sharpe, drawdown, and forward-live diagnostics can pass, but the aggregate stays `not_evaluable`, `full_size_allowed = false`, and limitations state that capacity / concurrency-adjusted returns are not evaluable. `tests.schema.test_execution_aggregate_report_schema` validates v1.1.2 and the updated full-size permission description.
- Required next action: no active `SR-EXEC-007` evidence-overclaim action. If future work wants true capacity-adjusted execution evidence, implement concurrent holdings, cash locks across holding windows, and continuous portfolio equity tests before removing the not-evaluable gate.

### SR-CAP-001 - Capital ceiling is not validated at state load / sizing boundary

- Severity: P1
- Status: resolved

- Evidence: `runners/backtest_execution.py:calculate_shares` caps by cash, bucket capital, max position percent, and max positions, but there is no hard validation that the loaded `bucket_capital` respects the market / bucket capital ceiling from policy.
- Accepted calibration: this is a missing validation / clamp, not proof that current fixtures always over-allocate. If state already has `bucket_capital <= ceiling_pct * market_capital`, the current calculation may be fine; if state is hand-edited above ceiling, no code rejects it.
- Closure evidence: the reviewed change set updates `runners/backtest_execution.py` to validate `capital_context.bucket_capital <= capital_context.market_capital * capital_context.bucket_ceiling_pct` when building the capital context and again before empty / simulated execution uses the bucket capital. Above-ceiling cash-state inputs now raise instead of entering share calculation.
- Verification: `tests.execution.test_backtest_execution` covers a hand-edited A-short cash state with `short_bucket_capital = 200000.0` against market capital `350000.0` and ceiling `0.333333`, expecting a `bucket_capital exceeds bucket ceiling` rejection. `tests.schema.test_execution_backtest_report_schema` and `tests.schema.test_capital_context_schemas` still pass.
- Required next action: no active `SR-CAP-001` action. If a later coordinator intentionally supports manual liquidity transfers or ceiling overrides, add a reviewed state transition and tests before allowing above-ceiling bucket capital into sizing.

### SR-RANK-001 - Forward-return status can remain `ok` when conversion leaves NaN

- Severity: P3
- Status: resolved
- Owner phase: rank backtest / forward-tracker compatibility
- Evidence: `runners/backtest_rank.py:attach_forward_returns` catches conversion exceptions and later assigns status `"ok"` even when return values can remain NaN.
- Accepted calibration: current rank statistics drop NaN values, so numeric contamination is low; a status-only consumer such as tracker / reporting code could still overread `"ok"`.
- Required next action: no active `SR-RANK-001` action. Future forward-return status changes must keep `"ok"` reserved for rows whose required return fields converted to finite numeric values.
- Closure evidence: `runners/backtest_rank.py:attach_forward_returns` now sets `pending_return_conversion_failed` and skips the `"ok"` status whenever required close-to-close or T+1 open-to-exit-close return conversion fails, produces NaN, or produces a non-finite value. `ret_*d_status = "ok"` is assigned only after both required return paths have converted successfully.
- Verification: `tests.test_backtest_rank_phase3` adds `test_forward_return_conversion_failure_is_not_ok_status`, proving a non-numeric exit close leaves return fields NaN and marks `ret_5d_status = pending_return_conversion_failed` instead of `"ok"`. `tests.phase6.test_forward_tracker_cache_guard` still passes, covering the status-consuming forward-tracker path.

### R-USSHORT-FORWARD-LIFECYCLE-MERGER-TICKER-SEMANTICS-UNRESOLVED - inactive status cannot safely identify a merger or successor ticker

- Severity: P1
- Status: open
- Owner phase: US-short active-only forward evidence / lifecycle containment
- Evidence: `runners/us_short_universe_fetch.py` already binds active-listing, halt, OTC, and bankruptcy status provenance into private candidate artifacts. The forward lifecycle slice adds `runners/us_short_forward_lifecycle_capture.py` and `schemas/us_short_forward_lifecycle_observation.schema.json`: a frozen private active-universe snapshot is compared only with a later private status-sourced candidate artifact. It retains the original frozen symbols and records `inactive_or_ticker_change_unresolved`, `halted`, `bankruptcy`, `otc_or_exchange_migration`, missing-current-row, or critical-status-unknown events as private manual-review/new-entry blocks. The disposition slice adds `engine/us_short_corporate_action_disposition.py` and `schemas/us_short_corporate_action_manual_disposition.schema.json`: only a separately source-bound, manually confirmed event can produce an exact stock/cash/manual-exit ticket. The offline identity/boundary slice adds CIK plus controlled share-class identity, a one-ticker manual-review freeze for source failure, and disabled yfinance/SEC interface skeletons. The manual event recorder transforms an explicitly confirmed human SEC transcription into the planner's exact event, accepts an EDGAR URL only when its CIK binds to the old or identity-bound successor security, and hashes rather than stores the URL; CVR and invalid/inconsistent input remain one-ticker review freezes. With the user-authorized account-state wiring, its runner reads a private local `us_short_account_state` only after explicit `--confirm-account-read`, extracts only the old ticker's validated long shares, emits only a digest binding, and writes the actual ticket only to a gitignored/external private path. The source-intake slice adds a default-dry-run, one-document SEC 8-K/8-K-A strict parser that emits only an unconfirmed candidate, plus a one-ticker yfinance split/dividend/source-availability alarm; complex/ambiguous SEC terms and any low-trust yfinance problem remain ticker-scoped review outcomes. The offline workflow slice adds an identity-bound, schema-validated one-command chain over lifecycle, SEC/yfinance, optional Massive diagnostic, the existing manual recorder, validated private account-state read, and the existing disposition planner. It emits a private ticket only after explicit human confirmation, requires a strict SEC candidate to match the confirmed event exactly, hashes the exact persisted ticket bytes, cleans partial outputs, and const-pins every automatic/paper/ship authority false. This implementation performed no live call, read no real account/raw artifact, confirms no SEC semantics, and changes no selection.
- Accepted calibration: an inactive listing or an absent current candidate can indicate delisting, ticker change, merger, acquisition, source outage, or candidate-artifact corruption. It is therefore a fail-closed trigger, not proof of a merger, a successor security, exchange ratio, cash consideration, effective date, or a tradeable exit price.
- Required next action: a strict parser candidate still requires a human to verify the specific SEC source and explicitly confirm old/successor security, effective date, stock/cash terms, and failure/unknown policy through the confirmed-event recorder; DEFM14A/CVR/complex or ambiguous terms remain fully manual. The currently available offline/manual engineering chain ends at a private disposition ticket. Any attempt to infer complex semantics, reconcile tolerances, or set the three §12.1 paper confirmations requires a separate reviewed contract and authorization. The authorized local account read remains read-only and private. No auto conversion, cash booking, forced exit, return calculation, selection/ranking change, DataHub, production, or ship-gate claim is allowed.
- Verification: `tests.provider.test_us_short_forward_lifecycle_capture` covers frozen-symbol retention plus inactive/ticker ambiguity, halt, bankruptcy, OTC, missing-row, unknown, malformed provenance, canonical-ticker, confirmation, and no-partial-write paths. `tests.test_us_short_corporate_action_disposition` covers all four event shapes, exact fractional stock entitlement, cents cash entitlement, source-confirmation/ticker/ratio/forced-exit rejection, and boundary-tamper rejection. `tests.test_us_short_corporate_action_event_recorder` covers account-state-only cash/stock/forced round trips, binding mismatch/no-position/malformed/nonlong rejection, confirmation, CVR/invalid freeze, identity binding, and old-or-successor SEC-URL CIK checks; its runner/schema suites pin opt-in account reading, private-ticket output, no account leakage, and confirmed/manual-review boundaries. The source-intake engine/runner/schema suites cover strict cash/stock/combined extraction, successor-filed identity binding, DEFM14A/CVR/adjustment/election/multi-value freeze, one-call authorization/URL/chronology preflight, no raw/URL/User-Agent output, yfinance clear/split/dividend/missing/mismatch/malformed neutralization, and const-false authority claims. The workflow engine/runner/schema suites cover evidence/identity/ticker/event binding, explicit confirmation/account-read gates, strict-candidate mismatch rejection, private-path/no-overwrite handling, exact ticket-byte digest binding, partial-output cleanup, forged authority rejection, and permanently blocked paper confirmations.
- Plain language: 股票从新名单消失时，系统会停下并要求人工核对；它不会擅自猜成并购、换成新股票、算现金，或把旧记录删掉。
